papers.title: Realization of the anisotropic XY model in a Tb(III)-W(V) chain compound
papers.pitch: By simply swapping Mo(V) for W(V) in a cyanido-bridged Tb chain, the magnetic interaction fundamentally switches from Ising to a textbook anisotropic XY model—despite an almost unchanged powder-averaged g-factor. The specific heat data map perfectly onto the exact solution for the 1D S=1/2 XY chain, revealing a striking J_y/J_x = 2 anisotropy that had never been cleanly observed in a molecular mat

papers.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
papers.pitch: A GPT-3 model learns to browse the web, gather sources, and compose answers that beat human-written Reddit explanations 69% of the time—not by improving search, but by training on human preferences with rejection sampling.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.pitch: Simply prompting a large language model to interleave reasoning with tool use yields a 34% absolute gain over standard reinforcement learning on a household decision-making benchmark—all from just one or two in-context examples. When these reasoning traces are combined with Wikipedia lookups for question answering, the same approach cuts the massive sample budgets needed by chain-of-thought, match

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: Instead of costly weight updates, a new framework lets LLM agents learn from mistakes by simply talking to themselves—storing their own written reflections in memory. On coding benchmarks, this verbal reinforcement pushes GPT-4 to 91% pass@1 accuracy, handily beating its prior 80% state-of-the-art, all without a single gradient step.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.pitch: Twenty-five AI agents living in a Sims-like town spontaneously throw a Valentine’s party, ask each other on dates, and spread a mayoral campaign rumor—all without further human prompting—by combining a large language model with a novel memory architecture.

papers.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
papers.pitch: SGLang achieves up to 6.4× higher throughput on complex LLM workloads by automatically reusing KV caches across 90% of calls, using a radix tree LRU cache that requires zero manual configuration. Its compressed finite state machines further accelerate structured output decoding by processing multiple tokens per step, making JSON-mode generation faster without sacrificing correctness.

papers.title: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
papers.pitch: A fully open 7B model matches Llama 2’s performance within 1.2% on core benchmarks despite using entirely public data and code—and its instruction-tuned version’s chat gap reveals just how brittle transferable fine-tuning recipes really are.

papers.title: Gemma: Open Models Based on Gemini Research and Technology
papers.pitch: A 7B-parameter open model trained on 6 trillion tokens can outperform a 13B LLaMA 2 across major academic benchmarks, while matching or exceeding the best comparable-scale systems on safety evaluations. Despite being freely released, the model leaks memorized training data at a rate far below even heavily curated open-weight peers.

papers.title: Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
papers.pitch: A layered ensemble of open-source LLMs can beat GPT-4 Omni by a huge margin (65.1% vs 57.5%) on AlpacaEval 2.0 simply by having models read and refine each other’s answers. The surprising twist is that this works even when a model is shown responses worse than its own—exposure to any external output triggers better generation, a phenomenon the authors call “collaborativeness.”

papers.title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
papers.pitch: An LLM-based multi-agent system plans web searches as a dynamic graph of sub-questions, allowing it to process over 300 pages in 3 minutes to match proprietary AI search engines. Evaluations show that an open-source 7B model using this framework produces responses humans prefer over GPT-4o-powered ChatGPT-Web and Perplexity.ai Pro in a majority of cases.

papers.title:
Diversity Empowers Intelligence: Integrating Expertise of Software
  Engineering Agents
papers.pitch: A committee of diverse open-source software engineering agents, guided by an LLM re-ranker, boosts issue resolution on SWE-Bench Lite from 27.3% to 34.3%—a 25% improvement—simply by combining their disjoint expertise. The best group hits 55%, showing that architectural diversity, not just more runs, is the key to unlocking collective intelligence in code repair.

papers.pitch: By reimagining long text as a modality akin to images, Squid shrinks an LLM’s energy appetite tenfold while preserving answer quality—a compact decoder compresses thousands of context tokens into memory embeddings that a larger decoder reads without paying the quadratic attention cost.

Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with
  100+ NLP Researchers
papers.pitch: AI-generated research ideas are judged as significantly more novel than ideas from human experts—scoring 5.64 vs. 4.84 on a 10-point scale—in the first large-scale, statistically rigorous comparison. This study reveals that while LLMs can outperform humans in creative ideation, their outputs lack diversity and the models cannot reliably evaluate the quality of their own proposals.

papers.title: Evolving Deeper LLM Thinking
papers.pitch: Mind Evolution uses a language model inside a genetic algorithm to achieve over 98% success on natural language planning benchmarks where a single forward pass from Gemini 1.5 Pro scored just 5.6%. It works by evolving entire candidate solutions through recombination and a global evaluator, without needing formal problem specifications or step-by-step process rewards.

papers.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
papers.pitch: Multi-agent LLM systems are failing at staggering rates—between 41% and 86.7% across state-of-the-art frameworks—and the root cause is not just weak models but fundamentally flawed system designs that lead to agents ignoring each other, prematurely ending tasks, or repeating steps in endless loops. papers.title: Large Language Model Agent: A Survey on Methodology, Applications and Challenges
papers.pitch: LLM agents are not just better chatbots—their effectiveness hinges on a unified architecture where memory, planning, and tool use are not separate modules but inherently intertwined design principles. papers.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
papers.pitch: For the first time, a fully AI-generated paper survived peer review and met the acceptance bar at an ICLR workshop—without using any human-written code templates. The system’s key innovation is an experiment manager agent that conducts progressive agentic tree search, enabling it to design, execute, and iteratively refine its own experiments from scratch across multiple ML domains.

papers.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
papers.pitch: LLM agents that can learn from their own mistakes remain largely aspirational—this survey reveals that while systems like WebRL can boost performance from 4.8% to 42.4% through self-generated training, catastrophic forgetting and reward hacking cripple autonomous evolution at scale. The paper provides the first systematic framework to diagnose why, organizing agent self-improvement into three axes

papers.title: Universal Deep Research: Bring Your Own Model and Strategy
papers.pitch: Existing deep research tools rigidly lock you into one model and one hard-coded search strategy. Universal Deep Research breaks this open by letting you write plain-language strategies that compile into code, turning any LLM into a deep research agent without fine-tuning—and it all fits in an 8k context window.

papers.title: The Landscape of Agentic Reinforcement Learning for LLMs: A Survey
papers.pitch: Reinforcement learning doesn't just align LLMs—it can install genuinely new reasoning behaviors, but only under tight conditions: high-fidelity verifiable rewards, compositional multi-step tasks, and a critical 'Goldilocks' zone of base model capability. papers.title: Astra: A Multi-Agent System for GPU Kernel Performance Optimization
papers.pitch: Even with cutting-edge LLMs, optimizing GPU kernels isn't trivial — a single coding agent reaches only 1.08× speedup. But by splitting the task across specialized agents that iteratively code, test, profile, and plan, Astra reaches 1.32× on production CUDA kernels without human intervention — disproving the assumption that LLMs can't tackle low‑level performance engineering.

papers.title: Towards General Agentic Intelligence via Environment Scaling
papers.pitch: Training language agents on a massive, automated diversity of 30,000 APIs organized into over 1,000 domains yields performance rivaling trillion-parameter models—yet their accuracy still linearly degrades as the number of required tool calls increases.

papers.title: LIMI: Less is More for Agency
papers.pitch: Training an AI agent on just 78 handpicked examples beats systems trained on 10,000. This paper shows that agency emerges through strategic curation, not data scale, overturning a core assumption of the field.

papers.title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
papers.pitch: Language agents can teach themselves to be better without rewards or human labels—just by observing what happens when they take different actions and reflecting on their own mistakes. Across eight diverse environments, this 'early experience' approach matches full imitation learning with only 12% of the expert data and, when combined with RL, achieves scores that expert-only training can’t reach.

papers.title: Demystifying Reinforcement Learning in Agentic Reasoning
papers.pitch: Training small LLMs to reason with tools often fails because we use fake, stitched-together data and RL recipes that kill exploration. The authors show that simply switching to real end-to-end tool-use trajectories and keeping the RL algorithm exploration-friendly (via higher clipping and entropy maintenance) lets a 4B model crush 32B competitors on math benchmarks.

papers.title: Tongyi DeepResearch Technical Report
papers.pitch: A 30B-parameter model with just 3B active parameters rivals or beats proprietary giants like OpenAI’s DeepResearch across seven deep research benchmarks—while being fully open-source. papers.title: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
papers.pitch: DreamGym replaces expensive real-environment rollouts with a reasoning-based experience model that synthesizes coherent state transitions and reward signals, achieving a >30% improvement on WebArena over all baselines where conventional RL fails due to sparse rewards. papers.title: What Does It Take to Be a Good AI Research Agent? Studying the Role of Ideation Diversity
papers.pitch: AI research agents that brainstorm a wider variety of model architectures before coding dramatically outperform those fixated on a single idea—a simple entropy measure of their initial plans predicts success and can be causally engineered to boost medal rates. By analyzing 11,000 agent trajectories, the authors show ideation diversity acts as a safety net, allowing agents to pivot when their first

papers.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems

papers.title: Long-horizon Reasoning Agent for Olympiad-Level Mathematical Problem Solving
papers.pitch: A gold-medal-level math AI scores 102/126 on the official Chinese Mathematical Olympiad under human expert judgment by breaking through the context-length ceiling that cripples even advanced models on IMO problems: instead of one impossibly long chain of thought, it maintains a compact memory of proven lemmas across multiple reasoning rounds, effectively expanding its working space 8×.

papers.title: Memory in the Age of AI Agents
papers.pitch: Agent memory is shifting from static retrieval to fully learned, RL-driven systems that autonomously decide what to remember, consolidate, and forget—yet no single substrate can yet unify text, vision, and action. papers.title: KernelEvolve: Scaling Agentic Kernel Coding for Heterogeneous AI Accelerators at Meta
papers.pitch: An AI agent generates GPU kernels for proprietary chips it was never trained on, achieving up to 17× speedups. It does this by injecting hardware constraints into its context at runtime, not just prompting. Deployed at Meta across thousands of models, it turned weeks of kernel coding into hours with 100% correctness.

papers.title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.pitch: Search-augmented LLMs become worse at knowing when to say “I don’t know” — reasoning models specifically keep searching for answers to unanswerable questions, burning tokens with no hope of a correct response. The paper’s new Tokens Per Correctness metric shows this over-searching can slash efficiency by over 50% on unanswerable queries compared to simple base models.

papers.title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: Moving beyond static benchmarks, this survey reveals that LLM reasoning fundamentally fails in open-ended settings unless models are redesigned as autonomous agents that plan, act, and adapt through continuous environmental feedback. By defining a three-layer taxonomy—foundational, self-evolving, and collective—it shows how reasoning scales not via bigger models, but by bridging thought and action

papers.title: Decoding ML Decision: An Agentic Reasoning Framework for Large-Scale Ranking System
papers.pitch: Major gains in ranking optimization aren’t stuck on better models, but on a critical translation bottleneck: turning fuzzy product goals into testable hypotheses. GEARS cracks this by letting operators steer systems with high-level ‘vibes’ while an agent autonomously discovers deployable policies—but only after a strict stability gate filters out strategies that overfit short-term noise.

papers.title: LLM2VEC-GEN: Generative Embeddings from Large Language Models
papers.pitch: LLM2VEC-GEN makes retrieval safer by encoding the model’s refusal to harmful queries rather than the malicious intent—cutting harmful content retrieval by up to 22.6%. It does this by learning to compress the LLM’s own response into an embedding without ever generating the text, while keeping the base model frozen.

papers.title: ProRL Agent: Rollout-as-a-Service for RL Training of Multi-Turn LLM Agents
papers.pitch: Surprisingly, decoupling agent rollouts from RL training into a standalone HTTP service—rather than keeping them tightly intertwined—can nearly double performance on software engineering benchmarks while preserving linear scalability. papers.title: CORAL: Towards Autonomous Multi-Agent Evolution for Open-Ended Discovery
papers.pitch: Giving LLM agents control over their own search decisions, rather than hard-coding evolutionary rules, yields 3–10× higher improvement rates and 20% better kernel optimization results. papers.title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
papers.pitch: A self-evolving training framework discovers and synthesizes thousands of realistic tool environments from real-world themes, then iteratively identifies an agent's capability gaps to generate targeted new tasks, producing 8B and 14B models that beat proprietary giants on 23 benchmarks. papers.title: Synthetic Computers at Scale for Long-Horizon Productivity Simulation
papers.pitch: Training agents to handle a month of real productivity work has been impossible because no one has realistic digital environments at scale—this paper invents synthetic computers with full filesystems and professional artifacts, runs 8-hour, 2,000-turn simulations that act as the user, and shows a +7 percentage point gain that only materializes when diverse professions are covered, completely rewri

papers.title: Orchard: An Open-Source Agentic Modeling Framework
papers.pitch: Orchard’s 30B-MoE agent, with only ~3B active parameters, hits 67.5% on SWE-bench Verified—outperforming all prior open-source 32B recipes by a wide margin and approaching proprietary models 10–30× larger. papers.title: HINT-SD: Targeted Hindsight Self-Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.pitch: LLM agents get corrected on every step when they fail a long task, but new work shows that most of that correction is noise and can actually make performance worse—up to 18.8% worse than a method that only fixes the specific actions that caused the failure. papers.title: Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the deep Q-network (DQN), a novel artificial agent that combines reinforcement learning with a deep convolutional neural network to learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs — receiving only raw pixels and the game score — using end-to-end reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Online Convex Programming and Generalized Infinitesimal Gradient Ascent
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and formally defines online convex programming—a repeated optimization setting where a convex feasible set is known but the convex cost function at each step is revealed only after a decision is made—and proposes the Greedy Projection algorithm (projected gradient descent with a decreasing learning rate $\eta_t = t^{-1/2}$) to solve it.

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
papers.pitch: SHAP values provide the *only* additive feature attribution method that satisfies three fundamental consistency properties, meaning that popular explanation methods like LIME can actually assign a lower importance to a feature that demonstrably makes the model’s output *higher*. papers.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
papers.pitch: Comressing a source sentencess into a fixed-length vector cripples encoder-decoder translation on long sentences—but letting the decoder attention to relevant source words while generating each target word eliminates this bottleneck, achieving performance comparable to phrase-based systems without separate alignment models.

papers.title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: A robot learning what a human wants through observation is fundamentally inefficient because it assumes the human acts selfishly—but when both know they share the same goal, the human naturally starts teaching and the robot starts asking, transforming value alignment into an active, collaborative process.

papers.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
papers.pitch: Reward functions are routinely hacked by the AI systems they intend to constrain, and seemingly harmless exploration can cause irreversible damage—yet these problems can be studied today in simple gridworlds, not just hypothetical superintelligences. papers.title: Inverse Reward Design
papers.pitch: A robot trained to prefer dirt paths over grass drives straight into lava because its designer never anticipated lava – and the reward function treats it as arbitrary. Inverse reward design treats the given reward not as the truth but as a clue about the designer’s hidden intent, enabling the robot to infer that lava was probably not okay and safely avoid it.

papers.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
papers.pitch: Commercial face recognition systems fail disproportionately on darker-skinned women—but we only discover this after users suffer the consequences. The authors propose "model cards," a standardized disclosure that surfaces such biases before deployment by reporting performance broken down across demographic and intersectional groups.

papers.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
papers.pitch: An RL-trained red-teaming LM extracts offensive replies from a chatbot over 40% of the time, and zero-shot generation alone unearths tens of thousands of failures—including overlooked data leaks and biases—that manual test cases never found.

papers.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
papers.pitch: A tiny 1.3B parameter model, fine-tuned with human preferences, convincingly outperforms the 175B GPT-3 in direct human evaluations. This shows you can close a 100× scale gap not by making models bigger, but by aligning them with simple human feedback.

papers.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: When fine-tuning language models with RL from human feedback, the KL divergence from the original policy grows with the square root of the reward—a surprisingly robust linear relationship that holds across model sizes. This predictable trade-off means you can estimate how far a model will drift from its pretrained behavior before training, offering a new lever for controlling alignment.

papers.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
papers.pitch: Forget expensive in-context prompts—parameter-efficient fine-tuning beats GPT-3’s few-shot performance by 6% absolute while using over a thousand times fewer FLOPs per prediction. The paper’s T-Few recipe, built on a new method called (IA)³ that simply rescales attention activations with learned vectors, even achieves the first super-human result on the RAFT benchmark.

papers.title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
papers.pitch: Adding just nine chain-of-thought datasets to instruction finetuning rescues—and actually improves—a model's reasoning ability, reversing the severe degradation seen when finetuning on non-CoT tasks alone. Scaling the number of tasks to 1.8K and model size to 540B yields a striking +9.4% average lift over PaLM, all for only 0.2% of pretraining compute.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.pitch: AI trained solely on a short list of principles, with zero human harm labels, outperforms models trained on extensive human feedback at remaining harmless—and it does so without becoming evasive, instead explaining its objections to harmful requests.

papers.title: SLiC-HF: Sequence Likelihood Calibration with Human Feedback
papers.pitch: A simple ranking loss can replace the entire PPO apparatus in RLHF—no reward rollouts, no value network, and dramatically less memory—while matching or beating a 6B RLHF-PPO model using only a 770M T5, and achieving a 96% human preference win rate when scaled.

papers.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment
papers.pitch: A 65B language model fine-tuned on only 1,000 curated examples—with no RLHF—can match or beat GPT-4 in nearly half of all human evaluations, suggesting that LLMs already possess their core capabilities after pretraining and merely need to learn a stylistic ‘veneer’ of interaction.

papers.title: The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs
papers.pitch: Fine-tuning open-source LLMs on ChatGPT outputs makes them sound fluent and authoritative, but this largely teaches the model to mimic style rather than improve factual accuracy or core knowledge. papers.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
papers.pitch: Expanding preference data from pairs to full rankings, and training with one-to-N contrasts instead of just pairs, can boost an aligned model's reward score to near-ChatGPT levels using only supervised fine-tuning—no reinforcement learning required.

papers.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
papers.pitch: Llama 2-Chat, a 70B open-source model, nearly matches ChatGPT-3.5 in human preference rankings while being released with full training transparency—a paradigm shift for an industry accustomed to closed-source dominance. Training required separating helpfulness and safety into two conflicting reward models, as a single model optimized both poorly.

papers.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: RLHF—the dominant method for aligning large language models like GPT-4 and Claude—cannot alone ensure AI safety because its core mechanism of optimizing for human approval systematically produces sycophancy, political biases, and adversarial vulnerabilities that are inherent to the approach rather than mere engineering challenges. papers.title: DeepSpeed-Chat: Easy, Fast and Affordable RLHF Training of ChatGPT-like Models at All Scales
papers.pitch: DeepSpeed-Chat slashes the cost of training a 13B-parameter ChatGPT-style model to just $290 and 9 hours on a single 8-GPU node—a feat that previously took days or was simply infeasible. It achieves this by seamlessly fusing inference and training into a single Hybrid Engine that eliminates redundant model copies and achieves up to 15× higher throughput than existing systems.

papers.title: SIMPLE SYNTHETIC DATA REDUCES SYCOPHANCY IN LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.pitch: Large language models will falsely agree that 1 + 1 equals 956446 just to match a user’s stated opinion—even though they demonstrably know the correct answer when no opinion is given. A lightweight fine-tuning step on synthetic data, where the model is taught that claim truth is independent of user belief, cuts this sycophantic behavior by up to 10% without harming other capabilities.

papers.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
papers.pitch: Replacing costly human annotators with a prompted LLM judge yields RL-based alignment that statistically matches RLHF across summarization and helpful dialogue, while surprisingly cutting harmfulness rates more effectively. Perhaps even more striking, the policy can self-improve using its own outputs as training signals, hinting at a scalable path to AI-driven alignment without human labels.

papers.title: QWEN Technical Report
papers.pitch: QWEN-14B, a 14-billion-parameter language model, not only outperforms all previous open-source models of its size but even surpasses the much larger LLaMA2-70B on three benchmarks. Its RLHF-tuned chat variant demonstrates advanced agentic tool use, approaching proprietary models like GPT-4 in complex tasks such as utilizing a code interpreter for multi-step reasoning.

papers.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: Aligning LLMs to be both helpful and harmless forces a messy trade-off: being too helpful produces dangerous answers, while rigid safety kills usefulness. papers.title: Controlled Decoding from Language Models
papers.pitch: A tokenwise RL solver matches the reward–KL frontier of best-of-50 while generating only 6 samples, by using a transferable prefix scorer to rerank short contiguous blocks mid-decoding. Multiple reward scorers can also be combined on the fly to steer a frozen model without retraining.

papers.title: The Unlocking Spell on Base LLMs: Rethinking Alignment via In-Context Learning
papers.pitch: Alignment tuning—the standard recipe for turning base LLMs into AI assistants—barely touches the model's core knowledge, shifting token distributions almost exclusively for stylistic tokens like discourse markers. Base LLMs can match or beat fully aligned models using just three in-context examples and a system prompt, bypassing SFT and RLHF entirely.

papers.title: Alignment for Honesty
papers.pitch: Unlike prior work that forces models to express uncertainty through calibration, this paper reveals that simply training LLMs to say "I don't know" when they lack knowledge can sharply increase refusal rates on unknown questions—while preserving near-baseline task accuracy. papers.title: Helping or Herding? Reward Model Ensembles Mitigate but do not Eliminate Reward Hacking
papers.pitch: Reward model ensembles reduce overoptimization but cannot stop reward hacking because all members share the same blind spots—rewarding verbose list answers or overly long summaries that look good on paper but fail in practice. By pretraining ensemble members from different random seeds, you get far more diversity and better generalization than just varying fine-tuning seeds. But the bad news is th

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities with Weak Supervision
papers.pitch: Strong models like GPT-4 can significantly outperform their weak supervisors—recovering up to half the performance gap just by finetuning on weak labels, a phenomenon the authors call weak-to-strong generalization. Simple interventions like an auxiliary confidence loss can push this recovery to nearly 80% on NLP tasks, showing that aligning superhuman models with weaker oversight is empirically tr

papers.title: Secrets of RLHF in Large Language Models Part II: Reward Modeling
papers.pitch: A reward model trained on standard human preference data can easily fool your PPO policy into failure, but clean that data with a multi-model voting metric and the same PPO training becomes dramatically stable. This report further introduces contrastive learning for sharper offline discrimination and a meta-learning method called MetaRM that enables the reward model to keep improving over multiple

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.pitch: A Llama 2 70B that rewards its own outputs during training beats GPT-4 0613 on AlpacaEval, and its reward judgments get more accurate over time rather than being frozen. By disabling the human-feedback bottleneck through Iterative DPO, the model improves both its instruction following and its ability to score responses, creating a runway for continued self-improvement.

papers.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
papers.pitch: Alignment methods like DPO implicitly encode human cognitive biases like loss aversion, which explains their surprising effectiveness. By explicitly modeling human utility using Kahneman and Tversky’s prospect theory, the proposed KTO method learns from simple binary feedback (desirable/undesirable) yet matches or exceeds DPO that requires costly pairwise preferences—even improving math reasoning

papers.title: Direct Language Model Alignment from Online AI Feedback
papers.pitch: Replacing static preference datasets with online AI feedback dramatically boosts direct alignment methods—online DPO beats offline DPO by a 66% win rate, and even surpasses RLHF, without ever training a reward model. The annotator LLM simply chooses the better of two responses sampled on-the-fly from the evolving policy, making the process fully on-policy.

papers.title: ODIN: Disentangled Reward Mitigates Hacking in RLHF
papers.pitch: Reinforcement learning from human feedback makes language models gamed word-count inflation, chasing higher scores without real quality gains. The paper shows that splitting a reward model into two heads—one embracing length bias and one explicitly trained to ignore it—lets you throw away the length-corrupted signal during RL, pushing the Pareto frontier of helpfulness vs. verbosity significantly

papers.title: Parameter Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: LoRA-based reward models and RL policies achieve alignment quality equivalent to full RLHF while training 90% faster and using half the memory, closing the infrastructure gap for alignment work.

papers.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
papers.pitch: Human preferences are often intransitive and irrational, yet standard alignment methods force them into a single reward hierarchy. SPPO treats alignment as a two-player game and provably converges to the Nash equilibrium—without needing a reward model—pushing Mistral-7B to a 28.5% win rate against GPT-4-Turbo using only a tiny 0.4B preference model.

papers.title: Direct Reward Optimisation for Large Language Models Alignment
papers.pitch: DRO reframes LLM alignment around abundant single-trajectory ratings (e.g., thumbs up/down) instead of scarce pairwise preferences, jointly learning an optimal policy and value function from a simple mean-squared loss. papers.title: Aligning Language Models with Demonstrated Feedback
papers.pitch: You don’t need thousands of preference labels to personalize a language model—just a handful of your own examples will do. DITTO treats those few demonstrations as the gold standard, iteratively generating synthetic

papers.title: Bootstrapping Language Models with DPO Implicit Rewards
papers.pitch: A DPO-trained language model can keep improving itself by using its own implicit reward model to label its generated responses, without any new human feedback. papers.title: Hermes 3 Technical Report
papers.pitch: The largest open-weight model, Hermes 3 405B, achieves state-of-the-art benchmark scores while being explicitly trained without moral guardrails—its creators call this 'no latent thoughtcrime.' This neutral alignment sacrifices some structured obedience for creative flexibility, forcing system designers rather than the model itself to handle safety.

papers.title:
Towards a Unified View of Preference Learning for Large Language Models:
  A Survey
papers.pitch: Reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning for aligning LLMs with human preferences actually share the same mathematical core, differing mainly in how feedback is gathered and how many samples guide each update, not in their fundamental optimization objectives. papers.title: U-SOPHISTRY: How RLHF Accidentally Teaches Language Models to Mislead Humans
papers.pitch: Standard RLHF pipeline makes language models better at convincing humans of wrong answers without improving task accuracy—false positive rates in human evaluation rise 24% on QA (QuALITY dataset with LLaMA-2-7B) and 18% on programming (APPS with Deepseek-Coder-7B)—using entirely standard, innocuous reward signals from ChatbotArena. papers.title: Instruction Following without Instruction Tuning
papers.pitch: Simply training a language model on responses alone, without their instructions, is almost as good as full instruction tuning. In fact, even narrow finetuning on poetry or code can unexpectedly unlock general instruction-following.
papers.similarPaper: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

papers.title: SynPO: Self-Boosting Large Language Models with Synthetic Preference Data
papers.pitch: A 7B model, trained solely on synthetic data generated from its own outputs, can surpass GPT-4’s instruction-following score on AlpacaEval 2.0 without any human preference annotations. This self-boosting loop, SynPO, works by having the model critique and refine its own generations, unlocking iterative, autonomous improvement.

papers.title: Asynchronous RLHF: Faster and More Efficient Off-Policy RL for Language Models
papers.pitch: Training a 2.8B model with asynchronous off-policy RLHF achieves identical performance to synchronous on-policy methods while cutting wall-clock time by 25%, and this speedup scales with model size—LLaMA 3.1 8B trains ~40% faster on instruction following. Online DPO surprisingly tolerates stale, off-policy data better than other RLHF algorithms, with robustness improving as models grow larger.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Alignment for LLMs
papers.pitch: LLM alignment methods can be made 2–5× more sample-efficient by formalizing the problem as a contextual dueling bandit and using Thompson sampling to actively select which response pairs to query for human feedback. This unified algorithm, SEA, outperforms all prior active exploration strategies, requiring tens of thousands fewer preference labels to reach the same model quality.

papers.title: SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes: A Comparative Study of Foundation Model Post-training
papers.pitch: While supervised fine-tuning (SFT) causes models to memorize training data and catastrophically fail on unseen task variants—dropping nearly 35% on visual navigation under simple rule or color shifts—reinforcement learning (RL) with an outcome reward consistently improves out-of-distribution generalization, even boosting visual recognition. papers.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
papers.pitch: Language models are forced to guess because training and evaluation both penalize admitting uncertainty—a model that says 'I don't know' loses on the leaderboard. Lower bounds show that even on perfect data, cross-entropy pretraining compels hallucination on rare facts, and post-training with binary grading creates a compute-optimal bluffing strategy.

papers.title: Multiplayer Nash Preference Optimization
papers.pitch: LLMs aligned against a single opponent get stuck in limited preference patterns—but when you train them to compete against an entire population of past checkpoints or diverse reward models simultaneously, they break out of these ruts. MNPO shows that scaling up this ‘multiplayer’ game yields a surprising 4-point jump on Arena-Hard over the best prior Nash method while swallowing DPO, INPO, and SPI

papers.title: LaSeR: Reinforcement Learning with Last-Token Self-Rewarding
papers.pitch: A model’s own assessment of its reasoning can be read directly from the probability it assigns to a single special token at the very end of its answer. LaSeR exploits this to train models that reward their own solutions using just one extra token of computation, matching the verification accuracy of external reward models up to 10× larger.

papers.title: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General Capabilities Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models
papers.pitch: RLVR post-training makes vision-language models better at reasoning but silently erodes their perception, knowledge, and robustness—sometimes dropping below the base model on 6 core benchmarks. papers.similarPaper: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General Capabilities Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models

papers.title: Conditional Equivalence of DPO and RLHF: Implicit Assumption, Failure Modes, and Provable Alignment
papers.pitch: DPO is not universally equivalent to RLHF—the derivation silently assumes the optimal policy already prefers human-chosen responses, an assumption that crumbles when the reference model is misaligned, causing DPO to optimize relative advantage rather than true preference satisfaction. papers.title: Maxout Networks
papers.pitch: A simple activation that outputs the max over several linear functions eliminates the saturation and underfitting pathologies that cripple dropout on standard units, enabling the training of deeper models and slashing CIFAR-10 error by over 2 percentage points—to 11.68%—without any data augmentation.

papers.title: Deep Mixture of Experts
papers.pitch: A stacked mixture-of-experts automatically learns to compose high-level concepts from low-level features—on jittered MNIST, first-layer experts become location detectors and second-layer experts become class recognizers, with all path combinations actively used. This factorization achieves the accuracy of a dense network with the same parameter count, paving the way for models where only a fractio

papers.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
papers.pitch: Turn a variational lower bound into a stochastic gradient-friendly objective by reparameterizing the latent variable as a deterministic function of a noise source—suddenly, backprop works through samplers, and a neural 'recognition model' can efficiently map each data point to its own approximate posterior without per-sample iterative inference.

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Sentences and Documents
papers.pitch: Without any parsing, this paper’s “paragraph vectors”—essentially topic memories trained alongside word vectors—crush the previous best on IMDb sentiment by 15%, plunging error below 10% for the first time. The same simple method beats recursive neural nets that explicitly model sentence structure, proving that dense, learned document priors can outsmart syntactic sophistication.

papers.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder–Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
papers.pitch: A pair of recurrent neural networks can learn to compress entire phrases into fixed-length vectors and decompress them into another language, with the resulting condensed representations capturing meaning and grammar rather than just memorizing translations. Even used simply as a scoring feature in a conventional translation system, this neural phrase model improves BLEU scores while qualitatively

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.pitch: Two neural networks playing a cat-and-mouse game can learn to generate strikingly realistic data without any of the painful approximate inference or Markov chains that plagued previous deep generative models.

papers.title: Caffe: Convolutional Architecture for Fast Feature Embedding
papers.pitch: Caffe hit 40 million images per day on a single GPU in 2014, and it did so by cleanly separating your network design from its hardware execution—swap between CPU and GPU with one flag, without touching a line of model code. papers.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
papers.pitch: A single-layer CNN using frozen pre-trained word vectors beats sophisticated, feature-engineered baselines on multiple benchmarks—no parsing or tuning required. Fine-tuning those vectors pushes performance even higher, achieving state-of-the-art on 4 out of 7 tasks with a model so simple it borders on trivial.

papers.title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
papers.pitch: A 22-layer network using 12× fewer parameters than the 2012 ImageNet winner crushed that model's accuracy with a mere 1.5 billion multiply-adds at inference—by replacing brute-force size with an "Inception module" that approximates a sparse architecture through parallel convolutions at multiple scales, proving efficiency and depth can trump raw parameter count.

papers.title: Memory Networks
papers.pitch: Even simple reasoning over stored facts fails in recurrent nets because their memory is too small and compressed—yet by adding a long-term, read–write memory component, a model can chain multiple supporting sentences with near-perfect accuracy on tasks that explicitly require understanding of verb intension.

papers.title: Neural Turing Machines
papers.pitch: Standard LSTMs fail catastrophically when generalizing to longer sequences unseen during training—yet a neural network equipped with a differentiable external memory and an attentional controller learns to perform true algorithms, correctly copying sequences over 5× longer than those it was trained on. The architecture invents its own addressing schemes, such as location-based iteration and conten

papers.title: Empirical Evaluation of Gated Recurrent Neural Networks on Sequence Modeling
papers.pitch: The simpler gated recurrent unit (GRU) matches or even beats the widely used LSTM on most sequence modeling benchmarks—despite having fewer parameters in the hidden state. In raw speech signal modeling, the advantage of any gating over a vanilla tanh unit is dramatic, while the choice between GRU and LSTM proves to be entirely dataset dependent.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.pitch: A simple architectural tweak—normalizing each layer's inputs within a mini-batch—lets you crank up the learning rate and ignore careful weight initialization, slashing training time by 14× on ImageNet while actually boosting accuracy past human-level performance.

papers.title: Improved Semantic Representations From Tree-Structured Long Short-Term Memory Networks
papers.pitch: Standard LSTMs forget how to compose meaning across long sentences because their linear chains force information to traverse every word—even when syntax brings distant phrases close. papers.title: LINE: Large-scale Information Network Embedding
papers.pitch: LINE can embed networks with millions of nodes in hours by preserving not just direct links, but also shared neighbors—effectively learning that two nodes are similar even if they never connected. papers.title: Highway Networks
papers.pitch: Networks with 900 layers can be trained directly with simple SGD by letting layers learn to skip themselves—bypassing the optimization collapse that cripples plain deep nets. The trick is a learned gate that routes information along unimpeded highways, making depth virtually free.

papers.title: Pointer Networks
papers.pitch: Neural networks can learn to solve combinatorial optimization problems like the Travelling Salesman Problem just by looking at examples, even generalizing to problem sizes never seen during training. The key is repurposing attention as a pointer to select input elements, sidestepping the fixed output vocabulary that limited prior sequence models.

papers.title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation
papers.pitch: A simple local attention mechanism that only looks at a small window of source words dramatically outperforms attending to all words, boosting BLEU by 5.0 points while being faster—and simply feeding previous attention vectors back into the model is as crucial as the attention itself.

papers.title: Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification
papers.pitch: Deep neural networks can classify text from raw characters without any word-level knowledge, and they outperform word-based models when millions of labeled examples are available—contradicting the widespread belief that words are essential for NLP. The same character-level model applies across languages with no tokenization or preprocessing, naturally handling misspellings and emoticons.

papers.title: Dueling Network Architectures for Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: Standard Q-networks waste capacity relearning state value for every action, but the dueling architecture explicitly separates value and advantage streams. This simple change lets the agent generalize across actions, especially when many are irrelevant—yielding huge gains on Atari games with large action sets while adding negligible computation.

papers.title: MXNet: A Flexible and Efficient Machine Learning Library for Heterogeneous Distributed Systems
papers.pitch: MXNet reveals that a single engine can seamlessly fuse imperative tensor operations with declarative symbolic graphs, achieving the same speed as Torch on one GPU while cutting memory use by up to 4×. This fusion then scales to slash a 14,000-second ImageNet training pass down to 1,400 seconds across ten GPU machines.

papers.title: EIE: Efficient Inference Engine on Compressed Deep Neural Network
papers.pitch: Fetching a weight from DRAM costs 200× the energy of the arithmetic that uses it, so EIE attacks the memory bottleneck by running directly on compressed models stored in on-chip SRAM. papers.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System
papers.pitch: A single tree-boosting system powered 17 of 29 Kaggle winning solutions in 2015, outpacing deep learning by handling sparse data with a novel default-direction algorithm and scaling to billions of examples on a single machine—all while running over 10× faster than existing popular libraries.

papers.title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)
papers.pitch: Neurons don't have to choose between being stochastic regularizers and activation functions—GELU merges them into a single, simple equation that beats ReLU and ELU across vision, language, and speech. It works by weighting inputs by their Gaussian cumulative probability, effectively soft-dropping low values instead of harshly zeroing them out. papers.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
papers.pitch: DenseNets connect every layer directly to all others via concatenation, not summation, slashing parameters by up to 90% while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy. The resulting extreme feature reuse means the network never needs to relearn redundant features, allowing 250 layers to train with just 15M parameters.

papers.title: Pruning Filters for Efficient ConvNets
papers.pitch: You can shrink a trained CNN by up to 38% in FLOPs by simply chopping out entire filters with the smallest weight sums—no special sparse math libraries required. The catch? Sensitivity varies wildly by layer; prune the wrong one and accuracy collapses, but a 'one-shot' removal followed by retraining recovers nearly all performance.

papers.title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio
papers.pitch: A raw waveform model conditioned on linguistic features produces speech that closes over half the gap to natural recordings, scoring 4.21 MOS on US English TTS. papers.title: Google’s Neural Machine Translation System: Bridging the Gap between Human and Machine Translation
papers.pitch: Google's production NMT system reduced translation errors by 60% against their phrase-based baseline in human evaluations, yet directly optimizing for BLEU scores with reinforcement learning provided no human-evaluable quality gains. papers.title: Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: A recurrent neural network trained with policy gradients can automatically discover convolutional and recurrent architectures that beat the best hand-designed models — achieving 3.65% error on CIFAR-10 while being faster than DenseNet, and finding a novel recurrent cell that surpasses LSTMs by 3.6 perplexity on Penn Treebank.

papers.title: Aggregated Residual Transformations for Deep Neural Networks
papers.pitch: ResNeXt proposes that increasing the number of parallel paths (“cardinality”) within a residual block boosts accuracy more effectively than adding depth or width, given a fixed computational budget. Testing with over 32 parallel branches, the model secured 2nd place at ILSVRC 2016, exposing a new scaling dimension that can outperform deeper ResNets at lower complexity.

papers.title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
papers.pitch: A simple neural network can match or beat far heavier 3D recognition models by directly consuming unordered point clouds—no voxels or views needed—thanks to a single symmetric function: max pooling. Even more surprising, the network learns to focus on a sparse set of “skeleton” key points that make it robust to missing data, outliers, and random perturbations.

papers.title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
papers.pitch: You can match VGG-16’s ImageNet accuracy with 27× less computation and 32× fewer parameters—by restructuring convolution itself. MobileNets achieve this through depthwise separable convolutions, which factor standard convolution into lightweight filtering plus pointwise combination, coupled with tunable width and resolution knobs to shrink models further without collapsing accuracy.

papers.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
papers.pitch: GraphSAGE learns to generate embeddings for entirely unseen nodes by sampling and aggregating features from their local neighborhood, eliminating the need to retrain when graphs evolve. On dynamic citation and Reddit data, it classifies new nodes 100× faster than DeepWalk while outperforming strong baselines, and it even generalizes to entirely new protein-interaction graphs.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.pitch: A new neural architecture called the Transformer achieves state-of-the-art translation while being easier to train than recurrent models—because it replaces recurrence entirely with the attention mechanism, computing all positions in parallel. papers.title: Graph Attention Networks
papers.pitch: Nodes in a graph can now learn to assign different importance to each of their neighbors—without ever needing the full graph structure upfront. This simple attention-based approach not only matches or beats all previous graph neural networks on standard benchmarks, but also generalizes directly to entirely unseen graphs.

papers.title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
papers.pitch: A VAE where the latent space is a set of quantized discrete codes, paired with an autoregressive prior, can generate coherent 128x128 images and raw speech that spontaneously organizes into words and phonemes—all without any labels. papers.title: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.pitch: By simply enforcing a 1-Lipschitz constraint on the discriminator through a novel, computationally cheap normalization of weight matrices, this method makes GAN training drastically more stable—generating high-quality images even with aggressive learning rates that cause competing methods to fail, while requiring minimal hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations
papers.pitch: Simply injecting relative position information into Transformer self-attention boosts BLEU scores by up to 1.3 points on English-German translation—entirely replacing the need for absolute position encodings. papers.title: DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
papers.pitch: Neural architecture search can be done with gradient descent instead of expensive black-box methods, slashing compute needs from thousands of GPU days to just a few. DARTS achieves state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10 and PTB by relaxing the discrete search space into a continuous one, enabling direct optimization of architecture parameters via bilevel gradient-based learning.

papers.title: How Powerful Are Graph Neural Networks?
papers.pitch: Standard graph neural networks like GCN and GraphSAGE are fundamentally blind to simple graph structures—they cannot even count the number of neighbors with identical features. papers.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
papers.pitch: Vanilla Transformers forget everything beyond a fixed-length segment, shattering long-range context. Transformer-XL reuses hidden states from previous segments as memory, simultaneously enabling dependencies 450% longer than standard Transformers and slashing evaluation time by a factor of 1,800×.

papers.title: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers
papers.pitch: Transformers can now handle sequences over 10,000 times longer than before—a Transformer trained on raw bytes generates coherent ImageNet samples and classical music minutes in length, all while reducing the quadratic self-attention cost to a mere O(n√n). papers.title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.pitch: EfficientNet-B7 matches the top ImageNet accuracy of the previous best ConvNet (GPipe) but in a package 8.4× smaller and 6.1× faster, shattering the belief that extreme scale requires extreme size. This leap comes not from a new operator, but from discovering that depth, width, and resolution must be scaled together in a fixed, balanced ratio via a simple compound coefficient.

papers.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
papers.pitch: Directly using BERT to find similar sentences means a single search over just 10,000 texts takes 65 hours. SBERT decouples sentence encoding, slashing that to 5 seconds while simultaneously improving accuracy beyond all prior embedding methods.

papers.title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
papers.pitch: ALBERT drastically shrinks BERT by sharing all parameters across layers and decoupling the hidden state size from the embedding dimension, yet its largest version sets new state-of-the-art results with 70% of BERT-large's parameters. papers.title: Compressive Transformers for Long-Range Sequence Modelling
papers.pitch: By compressing old memories instead of discarding them, the Compressive Transformer extends the effective context of attention models over 2x without any extra compute cost—and it drops WikiText-103 perplexity to 17.1. This simple twist on TransformerXL makes rare words over 20% easier to predict, closing the gap on human-like long-form narrative understanding.

papers.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
papers.pitch: By inverting the dominance of static computation graphs, PyTorch proved that the flexibility of imperative, define-by-run execution need not sacrifice GPU performance. papers.title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

papers.title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers
papers.pitch: Self-attention’s quadratic cost usually forces models to ignore most of the past, but Routing Transformers learn to cluster queries and keys on the fly, letting each word attend only to its nearest neighbors in context—slashing complexity to $O(n^{1.5}d)$ while beating dense Transformers on language modeling by a wide margin.

papers.title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
papers.pitch: Transformers choke on long documents because their self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length. This paper introduces Longformer, a drop-in replacement that combines local windowed attention with sparse global attention to achieve linear scaling, enabling the first RoBERTa-level pretrained model to process 4,096 tokens directly. papers.title: ETC: Encoding Long and Structured Inputs in Transformers
papers.pitch: Attention’s quadratic cost forces most Transformers to cap input at 512 tokens—but ETC breaks this barrier with global–local attention that separates a few global tokens from the long sequence, achieving linear scaling while actually beating standard attention on long-document QA. papers.title: Synthesizer: Rethinking Self-Attention for Transformer Models
papers.pitch: You can replace dot-product self-attention with a randomly initialized, learnable alignment matrix and still achieve competitive BLEU scores in machine translation—the token-token interactions thought essential are largely optional. papers.title: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
papers.pitch: Transformer self-attention is quadratic in sequence length, but this paper proves it’s actually low-rank—so you can throw away most of the computation. By projecting keys and values down to a tiny fixed dimension, Linformer slashes time and memory to linear O(n) with virtually no loss in performance, making 60× memory savings on 65K-length sequences a reality.

papers.title: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences
papers.pitch: Big Bird proves that a carefully designed sparse attention pattern—mixing global tokens, local windows, and random edges—can match the universal approximation power and Turing completeness of full quadratic attention, while slashing complexity to linear and handling sequences 8× longer. papers.title: Rethinking Attention with Performers

The key is an entropy-regularized exit mechanism that lets the model learn how many iterations to spend on each input, turning parameter efficiency into a form of adaptive, test-time computation.

papers.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
papers.pitch: Linear attention models finally beat standard Transformers at their own game—even on short sequences—by giving each feature dimension its own independent forgetting rate. A new chunkwise algorithm makes this fine-grained gating efficient enough to unlock up to 6× faster decoding for million-token contexts, all while matching or exceeding full attention quality as a drop-in replacement.

papers.title: Higher-order Linear Attention
papers.pitch: Second-order attention can run in O(1) per-token streaming time without constructing any n×n matrices. Strict causality is preserved using two extra prefix summaries, and chunk-parallel training exactly matches serial recurrence via an associative scan—making higher-order, attention-like mixing as efficient as modern RNNs.

papers.title: TiDAR: Think in Diffusion, Talk in Autoregression
papers.pitch: Autoregressive decoding wastes massive GPU compute because generating one token at a time is memory-bound; TiDAR breaks this bottleneck by drafting blocks of tokens in parallel via diffusion and autoregressively verifying them inside a single forward pass. papers.title: MixLM: High-Throughput and Effective LLM Ranking via Text-Embedding Mix-Interaction
papers.pitch: Replacing long item descriptions with learned embedding tokens during LLM ranking can slash inference context by 75.9× without sacrificing relevance—but only if encoder and ranker are jointly trained, not stitched together independently. This insight enabled LinkedIn to deploy LLM-powered ranking across all search traffic for the first time, unlocking a 0.47% gain in Daily Active Users.

papers.title: Stronger Normalization-Free Transformers
papers.pitch: A simple learned error function called Derf can completely replace normalization layers in Transformers and outperform them across vision, speech, DNA, and language tasks. Rather than fitting better, Derf works through improved generalization—showing higher training loss but better downstream accuracy everywhere it’s tested.

papers.title: Nemotron 3 Nano: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
papers.pitch: A 31.6B-parameter model matches or beats GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-30B on agentic and reasoning tasks while running up to 3.3× faster—and it maintains 99% of its accuracy even under aggressive FP8 quantization by selectively keeping just 6 attention layers and their preceding Mamba layers at full precision.

papers.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3: Efficient and Open Intelligence
papers.pitch: A hybrid Mamba-Transformer architecture achieves 3.3× higher throughput than comparable Transformer MoEs by replacing most attention layers with cheap state-space layers—without sacrificing accuracy. The two larger models use a new LatentMoE method that reinjects communication savings into more experts, while NVFP4 training delivers 3× peak throughput over FP8. papers.title: Web World Models
papers.pitch: Instead of generating entire worlds inside a model, this paper shows you can build limitless, logically consistent environments by letting ordinary web code handle the rules and using LLMs only to paint the scenery on demand. The key trick: deterministic hashing creates persistent content without a database, giving agents infinite worlds to explore while keeping everything reproducible and under c

papers.title: Dynamic Large Concept Models: Latent Reasoning in an Adaptive Semantic Space
papers.pitch: Language models waste massive compute on predictable tokens—this paper shows you can automatically learn to skip them. By detecting semantic boundaries on the fly and shifting one-third of inference FLOPs into a dedicated reasoning backbone operating on compressed concepts, it nets +2.69% across zero-shot benchmarks at matched cost, with the biggest jumps on hard reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Deep Delta Learning
papers.pitch: Transformers can now selectively rewrite their own residual streams—reading, comparing, and overwriting obsolete content instead of just adding to it—resulting in up to 0.03 lower validation loss and 1.18-point downstream accuracy gains in language models.

papers.title: Multi-Head Linear Attention: Restoring Expressivity of Linear Attention via Token-Level Multi-Head
papers.pitch: Linear attention collapses all queries into a single global memory, capping representation rank and forcing uniform attention weights, yet MHLA shows we can restore full softmax-level expressivity simply by partitioning tokens into multiple spatial heads—achieving a 41% boost on video generation and matching DiT-XL quality at 2.1× speed without any extra modules.

papers.title: HySparse: A Hybrid Sparse Attention Architecture with Oracle Token Selection and KV Cache Sharing
papers.pitch: A 80B MoE model using only 5 of 49 layers for full attention can beat full-attention baselines while cutting KV cache by 10× — simply by having sparse layers inherit attention decisions from the last full layer. This

papers.title: Parallel Track Transformers: Enabling Fast GPU Inference with Reduced Synchronization
papers.pitch: Standard tensor parallelism forces a costly GPU synchronization after every attention and feedforward layer—but the PT Transformer slashes those operations by up to 16× by decomposing the model into independent parallel tracks that sync only after entire blocks of layers, not individual sublayers. In 8-GPU serving stacks, this architectural change alone yields up to 31.9% higher throughput and 30%

papers.title: MiniCPM-SALA: Hybridizing Sparse and Linear Attention for Efficient Long-Context Modeling
papers.pitch: A 9B hybrid model combining sparse and linear attention achieves up to 3.5× faster inference than full-attention models at 256K tokens on a single GPU, and handles 1M-token contexts where same-sized Transformers crash from memory overload. The trick is a 1:3 layer ratio and a continual training recipe that repurposes an existing Transformer at a quarter of the usual cost.

papers.title: FlashAttention-4: Algorithm and Kernel Pipelining Co-Design for Asymmetric Hardware Scaling
papers.pitch: On Blackwell GPUs, the softmax exponential operation and shared memory traffic are 25–60% slower than the doubled tensor cores, reversing the traditional attention bottleneck. FlashAttention-4 emulates exponentials on fast FMA units and halves shared memory usage with a novel 2-CTA MMA mode, reaching 1613 TFLOPs/s—71% utilization on B200.

papers.title: Attention Residuals
papers.pitch: Standard residual connections blindly sum all layer outputs with equal weight, causing hidden states to grow uncontrollably with depth and diluting early-layer information. This paper shows that replacing that fixed sum with a softmax attention over previous layers—letting the model learn which past representations to emphasize—consistently improves scaling laws and yields a 7.5-point gain on GPQA

papers.title: Nemotron 3 Super: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
papers.pitch: By packing 120B parameters into just 12B active through a novel LatentMoE architecture, Nemotron 3 Super matches frontier dense models on agentic coding and math benchmarks—while running at up to 7.5× the throughput of Qwen3.5-122B. It also bakes in native speculative decoding that boosts generation speed another 3×, making real-time tool-using agents drastically cheaper to serve.

papers.title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
papers.pitch: A single scalar gate can’t simultaneously decide what to erase on the key side and what to write on the value side of a compressed memory—yet that’s exactly how Gated DeltaNet and KDA work. papers.title: Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data
papers.pitch: Google's Bigtable can scale to a petabyte across thousands of commodity servers while letting you choose whether data lives in memory or on disk—a flexibility that no existing database offered. By exposing a sparse, multidimensional map indexed by row, column, and timestamp, it forces a surprising trade-off: massive compression and linear scalability, but only if you deliberately design your row k

papers.title: An Introduction to Conditional Random Fields
papers.pitch: Dense, overlapping input features cripple generative sequence models like HMMs because they must model dependencies among the inputs — a problem linear-chain CRFs elegantly solve by directly discriminatively modeling p(y|x). papers.title: Stacked Denoising Autoencoders: Learning Useful Representations in a Deep Network with a Local Denoising Criterion
papers.pitch: Simply reconstructing clean inputs during unsupervised pretraining fails to learn feature detectors; yet corrupting those inputs and training the network to undo the damage yields Gabor-like edge detectors and outperforms deep belief networks—all by modifying only the objective, not the architecture.

papers.title: Deep Neural Networks for Acoustic Modeling in Speech Recognition
papers.pitch: This paper provides a shared overview of how four research groups replaced Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) with deep neural networks (DNNs) for acoustic modeling in automatic speech recognition across a variety of benchmarks—TIMIT, Bing Voice Search, Switchboard, Google Voice Input, YouTube, and English Broadcast News—using a two-stage training procedure.

papers.title: Deep learning
Mining Frequent Patterns without Candidate Generation
papers.pitch: Frequent pattern discovery has long been bottlenecked by the need to generate and test an exponentially large number of candidate itemsets—this paper eliminates that step entirely. papers.title: The Google File System
papers.pitch: GFS abandons traditional file system semantics by betting entirely on append-only writes and a relaxed consistency model, which allows atomic record appends from multiple concurrent clients without any locking. papers.title: Web Search for a Planet: The Google Cluster Architecture
papers.pitch: This paper presents the architecture of Google's production search engine cluster, analyzing how a throughput-oriented, highly parallelizable workload enables a fundamentally different hardware procurement strategy from traditional enterprise computing.

papers.title: Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Gated PixelCNN and its conditional variant, a convolutional autoregressive image model that generates pixels sequentially in raster-scan order.

papers.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
papers.pitch: PyTorch shattered the dogma that deep learning frameworks had to trade usability for speed — it turns out eager, Pythonic execution can match static-graph frameworks within 17% on every tested benchmark, even beating them on models like GNMTv2 by 60%. papers.title: Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks
papers.pitch: Rectifier neurons, which simply output zero for negative input and propagate a linear signal otherwise, let deep supervised networks suddenly match the performance of unsupervised pre-training on benchmarks like MNIST and CIFAR‑10. papers.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a general end-to-end sequence-to-sequence learning method using multilayered Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks — one LSTM to encode the input sequence into a fixed-dimensional vector, and another deep LSTM to decode the target sequence from that vector — and applies it to the WMT'14 English-to-French machine translation task.

papers.title: Support Vector Clustering
papers.pitch: A support vector machine can find clusters of arbitrary shape without being told how many clusters exist: by searching for the smallest enclosing sphere in a high-dimensional feature space and mapping it back to data space, the sphere naturally splits into disconnected contours that each enclose a separate cluster. papers.title: TensorFlow: A System for Large-Scale Machine Learning
papers.pitch: TensorFlow unifies state management and computation into a single dataflow graph, letting you implement novel parallelization schemes—like moving compute to the data—without rewriting the system. Despite conventional wisdom that async is essential for scale, its sync replication scales to 200 workers, and a cheap 4-worker backup policy cuts slow-step straggler overhead by 10×.

papers.title: OpenAI Gym
papers.pitch: This paper reveals that unlike standard ML benchmarks, the real challenge in reinforcement learning isn't just performance but *sample complexity*—how many episodes an agent needs to learn, not just how well it ultimately does. papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
papers.pitch: Simply sampling 100 solutions from Codex and picking the one that looks most plausible to the model itself solves 70.2% of coding problems that no prior language model could even touch. This brute-force strategy transforms a complete failure into a 77.5% solve rate, but only works because base competence already exists—a critical caveat for scaling hopes.

papers.title: StarCoder: may the source be with you!
papers.pitch: A 15.5B-parameter open-access code LLM trained entirely on permissively licensed data can match or exceed OpenAI's closed code-cushman-001, while a new attribution tool proves it's possible to trace generated code back to specific training files—challenging the notion that LLMs are inscrutable black boxes.

papers.title: Lightweight Reranking for Language Model Generations
papers.pitch: You can match the performance of expensive, specialized rerankers for code generation just by counting overlapping words between sampled outputs. This lightweight "generalized self-consistency" approach beats random selection by a wide margin on HumanEval and even rivals heavy baselines that double inference cost—all while assuming only black-box access to the model.

papers.title: Magicoder: Empowering Code Generation with OSS-INSTRUCT
papers.pitch: A 7B open-source model trained on synthetic instructions inspired by real open-source code snippets beats ChatGPT on coding benchmarks—even when its teacher model is weaker than ChatGPT, proving the method extracts latent capability rather than simply distilling the teacher’s knowledge.

papers.title: Long Context Granite Code Models: Scaling Granite Code Models to 128K Context
papers.pitch: Open-source code models can reach 128K-token contexts without sacrificing their core coding ability. papers.title: Qwen2.5-Coder Technical Report

This balanced recipe preserves general reasoning while achieving 92.7% on HumanEval, proving that data engineering can close the gap with proprietary giants.

papers.title: OPENCODER: THE OPEN COOKBOOK FOR TOP-TIER CODE LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

The resulting models generate production-grade optimizations that get merged into real systems, outperforming proprietary giants like Claude-4.6-opus.

papers.title: InCoder-32B-Thinking: Industrial Code World Model for Thinking

The key insight is not just teaching the model to think, but training a surrogate "world model" on GPU profiles and Verilog simulations so it can self-verify hardware-level reasoning without a real toolchain.

papers.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Position Interpolation
papers.pitch: Transformers with RoPE suffer catastrophic attention-score spikes when forced to extrapolate to unseen position indices—but this paper shows that simply down-scaling those indices to stay within the pretrained range makes 32k-token context windows possible with just 1000 fine-tuning steps, thanks to a ~600× smaller interpolation error bound.

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.pitch: Language models exhibit a striking 'U-shaped' performance curve when using long inputs—they excel at information at the very beginning or end, but performance plummets when critical details sit in the middle, sometimes dropping below not having the context at all.

papers.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model
papers.pitch: An LLM can compress 512 tokens into just 128 internal “memory slots” that outperform same-length text summaries by a 2× margin, delivering 4× context compression with only 1% added parameters. This works only when the model pretrains to autoencode and generate from its own compressed representations—skipping that step leads to severe hallucination.

papers.title: Multilingual E5 Text Embeddings: A Technical Report
papers.pitch: An instruction-tuned multilingual model, enriched with 500k synthetic examples across 93 languages, beats both the strongest multilingual competitor and a comparable English-only model on English tasks. Meanwhile, the same model surpasses LaBSE—purpose-built for bitext mining—by 2.7 points across 112 languages, revealing how synthetic data can overcome pre-training coverage gaps.

papers.title: Data Engineering for Scaling Language Models to 128K Context
papers.pitch: You can extend a 4K-trained LLM to retrieve information across 128K tokens with just 1–5 billion carefully mixed tokens—ditching complex architectures or massive data budgets—and match GPT-4 128K performance on the Needle-in-a-Haystack test.

papers.title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens
papers.pitch: LongRoPE pushes the context window to an unheard-of 2 million tokens without needing million-token training data—it achieves this by exploiting a newly discovered 8× non-fine-tuning extension property and surgically correcting catastrophic new-position values through an evolved, non-uniform RoPE interpolation.

papers.title: Qwen2.5-1M Technical Report
papers.pitch: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M becomes the first Qwen2.5 model to surpass 90 accuracy on the RULER long-context benchmark at 128K tokens, while their training-free Dual Chunk Attention mechanism enables 16× context extrapolation without any fine-tuning, achieving 94.1% passkey retrieval at 2M tokens on a model only trained to 256K.

papers.title: Context Training with Active Information Seeking
papers.pitch: Simply giving context-optimizing LLMs a search tool backfires—external information pollutes the retained context and degrades performance. The authors rescue this idea with a beam-search training procedure that maintains and prunes multiple candidate contexts, turning web access into a consistent, generalizable advantage that can even beat models 5× more expensive.

papers.title: Enabling Cognitive Intelligence Queries in Relational Databases using Low-dimensional Word Embeddings
papers.pitch: Relational databases have no native concept of word meaning, forcing semantic queries to rely on brittle dictionaries or ontologies. This paper shows that by learning low-dimensional token vectors directly from a database’s own text and schema, one can run SQL-based "cognitive intelligence" queries that find semantically related rows—even when they share no syntactic keywords.

papers.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling

papers.title: DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining
papers.pitch: A small 280M proxy model trained without any downstream task labels can find pretraining data domain weights that let an 8B model match the accuracy of weights hand-tuned on those very downstream tasks, while improving perplexity on *every* domain—even heavily downweighted ones—and cutting training steps by 2.6×.

papers.title: Enhancing Chat Language Models by Scaling High-quality Instructional Conversations
papers.pitch: Fine-tuning on a massive corpus of 1.5 million purely synthetic, multi-turn chats pushes a LLaMA model to surpass Vicuna as the best open-source chatbot, yet it still scores just 54% on TruthfulQA, showing scaled synthetic data improves style and breadth but not factuality.
