papers.title: Quartet II: Accurate LLM Pre-Training in NVFP4 by Improved Unbiased Gradient Estimation
papers.pitch: Simply replacing element-wise stochastic rounding with a microscaling-aware routine cuts NVFP4 gradient error by more than half, unlocking up to 4.2× GPU speedups with far smaller accuracy sacrifice than previously thought possible.

papers.title: Golden Goose: A Simple Trick to Synthesize Unlimited RLVR Tasks from Unverifiable Internet Text
papers.pitch: Training on just 25% of available RLVR data actually improves the model while the rest causes degradation—revealing that effective problem-solving hinges on encountering genuinely novel reasoning patterns rather than more data. Golden Goose unlocks unlimited such patterns by turning any text’s missing reasoning steps into multiple-choice questions, generating over 700K fresh tasks that revive satu

papers.title: Decouple Searching from Training: Scaling Data Mixing via Model Merging for Large Language Model Pre-training
papers.pitch: DeMix finds optimal data mixtures for LLM pre-training without training proxy models, by simply merging a few specialized component models together. This decoupling achieves the same accuracy as prior search methods at a fraction of the compute cost and demonstrates, for the first time, that linear model merging reliably predicts the effects of data mixing at scale.

papers.title: Self-Hinting Language Models Enhance Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: On hard prompts, GRPO silently collapses: when no rollout in a group succeeds, advantage estimates vanish and the model stops learning. SAGE injects self-generated hints during training—lossy compressions of reference solutions—to rescue within-group outcome diversity under the exact same reward function, yielding consistent gains (e.g., +2.0 on Llama-3.2-3B) while requiring zero privileged inform

papers.title: LLaDA2.1: Speeding Up Text Diffusion via Token Editing
papers.pitch: LLaDA2.1 turns the classic speed–quality trade-off in large diffusion language models on its head by letting the model retroactively edit its own mistakes. A 100B model hits 892 tokens per second on coding tasks by drafting aggressively and then fixing errors on the fly, effectively making parallel generation both fast and accurate.

papers.title: A 3B Model Now Executes 600-Step Deep Searches and Beats 30B Models at Code—Without Tradeoffs
papers.pitch: Nanbeige4.1-3B demonstrates that a 3B generalist model can execute stable multi-turn agentic searches over 600 tool-call turns—an ability absent in models up to 8B parameters—while simultaneously achieving code generation scores that surpass Qwen3-30B-A3B. The key is a credit assignment strategy that combines point-wise and pair-wise rewards with turn-level supervision on synthesized deep-search t

papers.title: Task-Targeted Embedding Distillation (jina-embeddings-v5-text)
papers.pitch: Mixing distillation with single-task LoRA adapters, not joint multi-task training, is what resolves the stubborn conflicts between retrieval, similarity, and classification objectives—enabling a 239M-parameter model to outperform everything under 500M parameters on multilingual benchmarks.

papers.title: CUDA Agent: Large-Scale Agentic RL for High-Performance CUDA Kernel Generation
papers.pitch: A language model trained with reinforcement learning in an interactive CUDA development environment generates kernels that dramatically beat torch.compile, where even the strongest proprietary models fail. By giving the model profiling tools and execution feedback, it learns to discover algebraic simplifications and novel tiling strategies that static compilers miss, more than doubling the geometr

papers.title: Qwen3-Coder-Next Technical Report
papers.pitch: An 80B-parameter coding agent model that activates only 3B parameters per inference matches the performance of models over ten times its size on SWE-Bench Pro by scaling agentic training with verifiable, environment-feedback-driven reinforcement learning.

papers.title: In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Tool Use in Large Language Models
papers.pitch: ICRL shows that large language models can master tool use without any supervised fine-tuning data. By simply showing a few examples inside the RL training rollouts and then gradually removing them, models leap from imitation to autonomous tool calling. This pure RL approach slashes data costs and beats traditional SFT+RL pipelines by up to 9 points on knowledge-intensive benchmarks.

papers.title: How Far Can Unsupervised RLVR Scale LLM Training?
papers.pitch: All intrinsic reward methods for unsupervised LLM reinforcement learning inevitably collapse, not due to engineering flaws but because they mathematically sharpen the model's initial beliefs—amplifying correct predictions early and wrong ones later. External reward methods exploiting compute asymmetries (easy to verify, hard to generate) show they can escape this ceiling entirely. The new Model Co

papers.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Self-Reflection for Agentic Search
papers.pitch: Search agents trained with standard RL often plateau on mediocre strategies because they only receive a sparse reward at the very end. MR-Search breaks this deadlock by having the agent explicitly write a self-reflection after each failed episode and feeding it into the next attempt, coupled with a training algorithm that assigns credit at every intermediate turn. This simple loop—try, reflect, re

papers.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning versus Reinforcement Learning: A Study of Post-Training Methods for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: LLM post-training has undergone a decisive paradigm shift—hybrid SFT+RL pipelines exploded from just 20% of studies in 2023 to 73.8% in 2024. This survey reveals that SFT and RL are not separate stages but deeply connected under a unified gradient framework, where SFT is simply RL with an implicit trajectory-reproduction reward.

papers.title: Nemotron-Cascade 2: Post-Training LLMs with Cascade RL and Multi-Domain On-Policy Distillation
papers.pitch: A 30B MoE model with just 3B active parameters achieves Olympic-level reasoning—gold medals at IMO 2025, IOI 2025, and ICPC World Finals—matching 20× larger systems. The key is aligning multi-domain RL stages with on-policy distillation from specialized teachers, crushing the usual trade-off between reasoning prowess and general instruction-following.

papers.title: A Survey of On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: Training smaller language models by imitating fixed teacher outputs causes errors to compound quadratically with sequence length. On-policy distillation fixes this by having the teacher correct what the student actually generates, reducing the error growth to linear and reframing the entire process as iterative correction. This survey unifies the scattered design choices—from divergence selection

papers.title: SandMLE: A Multi-Agent Framework that Generates Synthetic Sandbox Environments for Training Machine Learning Engineering Agents
papers.pitch: Training ML engineering agents with on-policy RL was infeasible because verifying a single solution requires training a full model on millions of samples. SandMLE makes it possible by generating diverse, micro-scale synthetic tasks of just 50–200 samples, slashing execution time by 13× while preserving the mathematical complexity needed for agents to learn, leading to massive gains over supervised

papers.title: RAGEN-2: Reasoning Collapse in Agentic RL
papers.pitch: LLMs trained with RL can appear fine—stable entropy, good rewards—while secretly adopting input-blind reasoning templates that look diverse per prompt but never actually respond to what you ask. The paper demonstrates this "template collapse" is invisible to standard monitoring, proposes a mutual-information proxy that catches it in real time, and shows that filtering training data by reward varia

papers.title: SFT Does Generalize — But Only If You Train Long Enough, Use Verified CoT Data, and Start Stronger
papers.pitch: Reasoning supervised fine-tuning isn’t doomed to memorization: cross-domain performance actually follows a *dip-then-recover* pattern, where early under-optimization is routinely mistaken for generalization failure.  Verified long chain-of-thought traces can even teach a strong model transferable backtracking skills from a toy arithmetic game, reframing the narrative from “does it generalize?” to

papers.title: FP4 Explore, BF16 Train: Diffusion Reinforcement Learning via Efficient Rollout Scaling
papers.pitch: Quantized FP4 rollouts can match BF16’s alignment performance while accelerating diffusion RL convergence up to 4.64×, provided the policy is only trained on high-precision regenerations of the contrastive samples. The paper resolves the longstanding tension between scalable exploration and training stability by decoupling these stages completely, demonstrating that intra-group reward ranking rema

papers.title: Self-Distillation Zero: Self-Revision Turns Binary Rewards into Dense Supervision
papers.pitch: Even a wrong answer contains useful information. SD-ZERO shows that by training a model to revise its own incorrect responses—then distilling that revision ability back into the base generator—you can convert a single binary reward into dense, token-level supervision, dramatically boosting sample efficiency and beating standard RL with zero external data.

papers.title: Lightning OPD: Efficient Post-Training for Large Reasoning Models with Offline On-Policy Distillation
papers.pitch: On-policy distillation can be done completely offline—and actually works—as long as you use the same teacher for both SFT and distillation. Violating this "teacher consistency" was the hidden reason previous offline attempts failed. Lightning OPD exploits this insight to match standard OPD's accuracy while slashing training cost by 4×, even scaling to MoE models on a single node.

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
papers.pitch: A stronger teacher (DeepSeek 7B) can completely fail to improve a student (DeepSeek 1.5B) through on-policy distillation, while a weaker, RL-trained version of the same 1.5B student succeeds—revealing that the teacher's thinking patterns must overlap with the student's for OPD to work. The entire effect is driven by progressive alignment on a tiny fraction of high-probability tokens, raising the c

papers.title: Pre-train Space Reinforcement Learning: From P(y|x) to P(y)
papers.pitch: Optimizing the marginal token distribution P(y) prunes entire incorrect reasoning subspaces and spontaneously amplifies reflective behaviors like self-correction by over 14×—without ever seeing a task prompt. This 'Negative Sample Reinforcement' effect can bootstrap post-training RL, yet too much pre-train RL produces over-exploratory models that sabotage downstream optimization.

papers.title: Listwise Policy Optimization: Group-based RLVR as Target-Projection on the LLM Response Simplex
papers.pitch: Standard group-based RL for LLMs, like GRPO, is secretly just a crude first-order guess at projecting the policy toward an implicit reward-weighted target—and the authors show you can compute that projection exactly on the sampled response simplex, yielding bounded, self-correcting gradient coefficients. Listwise Policy Optimization decouples the target distribution from the divergence used to rea

papers.title: PyTorch FSDP: Experiences on Scaling Fully Sharded Data Parallel
papers.pitch: PyTorch FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel) introduces a native, production-grade solution for efficiently training enormous deep learning models that cannot fit on a single GPU—by sharding parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across devices, and only gathering full parameters as needed. Co-designed with PyTorch's core internals for plug-and-play usability, FSDP enables users to scale model

papers.title: A decision-theoretic generalization of on-line learning and an application to boosting
papers.pitch: The multiplicative weight-update rule, famous for mastering worst-case binary prediction, is shown to drive a far more general class of on‑line decision problems—from portfolio gambling to repeated games—without statistical assumptions. Crucially, this same framework yields a new boosting algorithm that works without ever knowing the weak learner’s error rate in advance.

papers.title: Adaptive Subgradient Methods for Online Learning and Stochastic Optimization
papers.pitch: Infrequent but highly predictive features are systematically overlooked by standard gradient methods; this paper shows how to automatically assign per-feature learning rates based on past gradient history, provably outperforming any fixed proximal function chosen in hindsight. The resulting ADAGRAD algorithm yields regret bounds that scale with the per-coordinate gradient norms, dramatically impro

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.pitch: Simply inserting a normalization step into a deep network lets it train 14x faster and eliminates the need for Dropout—all while surpassing human-level accuracy on ImageNet. The key insight is that the shifting distributions of layer inputs during training, what the authors call internal covariate shift, is the primary bottleneck, and addressing it via per-mini-batch normalization that backpropaga

papers.title: Large Scale Distributed Deep Networks
papers.pitch: Training a neural network 30x larger than any before it—1.7 billion parameters—is not only possible but practical using asynchronous SGD with thousands of CPU cores. This massive scale delivers state-of-the-art ImageNet accuracy, while on a speech task the same distributed approach hits target quality over 10x faster than a GPU.

papers.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
papers.pitch: Randomly dropping half the neurons during training forces the network to learn robust features that work well with many random subsets of other neurons, drastically reducing overfitting. At test time, this otherwise impossible ensemble of exponentially many sub-networks is approximated simply by halving the weights—giving state-of-the-art results on MNIST, ImageNet, and speech recognition with vir

papers.title: Regularization and Variable Selection via the Elastic Net
papers.pitch: The elastic net simultaneously selects variables and encourages correlated predictors to enter the model together—a feat the lasso cannot accomplish when data is scarce. In the p > n regime, it overcomes the lasso's hard saturation limit, selecting entire gene pathways rather than arbitrary single representatives.

papers.title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks
papers.pitch: Randomly initialized deep networks fail not just because gradients vanish, but because the standard initialization actually causes gradients to shrink exponentially across layers—and the logistic sigmoid’s non-zero mean actively drives top layers into saturation. By analyzing variance flow in both directions, the authors derive a normalized initialization that fixes this, matching the performance

papers.title: Adapting Large Language Models for Document-Level Machine Translation
papers.pitch: Fine-tuning a 7B LLM can beat GPT-4 on document-level translation, but a shocking failure mode emerges: up to 98% of outputs are in the wrong language due to error propagation during decoding, where a single mistake poisons the entire document.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning Using Gaussian Fields and Harmonic Functions
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a semi-supervised learning framework based on a Gaussian random field model defined over a weighted graph connecting labeled and unlabeled instances, where the most probable configuration — the graph's harmonic function — has a unique closed-form solution efficiently computable via matrix methods or belief propagation.

papers.title: Hogwild!: A Lock-Free Approach to Parallelizing Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.pitch: Ditching locks entirely in parallel stochastic gradient descent actually works—and it’s not just a hack. When your problem is sparse, meaning each gradient update touches only a tiny slice of the parameter vector, the chance of processors corrupting each other’s progress is so low that Hogwild! achieves a near-optimal convergence rate, delivering an order-of-magnitude speedup over lock-based syste

papers.title: Least Angle Regression
papers.pitch: LARS computes the full Lasso solution path at the same computational cost as a single ordinary least-squares fit, slashing runtime by an order of magnitude. The algorithm reveals that two seemingly distinct model selection methods—Lasso and Forward Stagewise—are just constrained versions of the same equiangular building strategy.

papers.title: Map-Reduce for Machine Learning on Multicore
papers.pitch: A wide swath of machine learning algorithms—from SVMs to backpropagation—can be rewritten into a single, exact 'summation form' that delivers near-linear speedups as you throw more processor cores at the problem, without any per-algorithm cleverness.

papers.title: Regularized Multi-Task Learning
papers.pitch: Learning multiple related tasks jointly beats learning them independently—but only when they truly share structure. This paper extends SVMs to multi-task learning by decomposing each task into a shared and an individual component, with a coupling parameter that controls how strongly tasks influence one another, showing the largest gains precisely when task similarity is high.

papers.title: On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning
papers.pitch: Carefully tuned SGD with momentum can train deep and recurrent nets from scratch, matching or beating complex second-order methods—but only when a very specific initialization *and* a slowly increasing momentum schedule are used together; miss either, and performance collapses.

papers.title: Netflix Update: Try This at Home
papers.pitch: A few hundred lines of code, training one SVD feature at a time with simple gradient descent and aggressive regularization, can predict movie ratings well enough to enter the Netflix Prize top three—without needing to store or factor the full 8.5-billion-entry matrix.

papers.title: Online Convex Programming and Generalized Infinitesimal Gradient Ascent
papers.pitch: Simple gradient-based algorithms can achieve no-regret outcomes even in adversarial, unknown environments—without any statistical assumptions about the sequence of cost functions. This work proves that projected gradient descent with a carefully chosen decreasing step size guarantees vanishing average regret against arbitrary convex loss sequences, and it establishes GIGA as the first universally

papers.title: Some PAC-Bayesian Theorems
papers.pitch: You can tune a learning algorithm with a rich prior encoding all your domain knowledge and still get the standard PAC guarantee that it won’t catastrophically overfit—even when that prior is completely wrong. This paper proves that an error bound scaling with the prior probability of a concept set replaces VC dimension entirely, combining Bayesian specificity with distribution-free reliability.

papers.title: Pegasos: Primal Estimated sub-GrAdient SOlver for SVM
papers.pitch: Stochastic sub-gradient descent can solve SVMs in O(1/ε) iterations, not O(1/ε²)—a quadratic improvement that makes the runtime independent of training set size for linear kernels. The Pegasos algorithm achieves this by using a carefully timed learning rate of 1/(λ t), delivering order-of-magnitude speedups over cutting-plane methods on large text datasets.

papers.title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: A single agent stacking six separate DQN improvements matches the original DQN's final performance using only 3% of the training data, and ultimately more than triples the median human-normalized score across 57 Atari games—proving these innovations are not just individually useful but strikingly complementary. Surprisingly, the ablation shows that removing prioritized replay or multi-step learnin

papers.title: Random Forests
papers.pitch: This paper introduces random forests, a classifier consisting of an ensemble of tree-structured classifiers where each tree is grown using a random vector sampled independently from the same distribution, with the forest voting for the most popular class.

papers.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
papers.pitch: A neural network can translate English to French better than a phrase-based system by simply reading the input sentence backwards. Reversing the source word order shrinks the gap between corresponding words, turning a difficult long-range dependency problem into one dominated by short-term dependencies that the LSTM solves easily.

papers.title: Large-Scale Machine Learning with Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.pitch: Contrary to the optimization dogma that better convergence rates per iteration yield better learning, stochastic gradient descent—one of the poorest optimizers—achieves the fastest *statistical* convergence when data is abundant because the learning problem is bounded by computation time, not sample size. In this regime, a single pass through the data with averaged SGD is already asymptotically ef

papers.title: Support Vector Machine Learning for Interdependent and Structured Output Spaces
papers.pitch: Standard SVMs treat class labels like black boxes—swapping classes 3 and 7 carries the same penalty as any other mistake. This paper shows how to bake the geometry of your output space into the SVM itself, achieving a 71-point reduction in sequence alignment error and a 5–7% accuracy jump in taxonomic classification by making the margin respect structured, user-defined losses.

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality
papers.pitch: Adding just two word vectors—like “Germany” and “capital”—yields a vector closest to “Berlin,” challenging the need for complex compositional models. The same Skip-gram architecture can learn meaningful representations for millions of phrases, treating “Air Canada” as a single token identified by a simple, data-driven method.

papers.title: Intriguing properties of neural networks
papers.pitch: Deep neural networks are easily fooled: an imperceptible, carefully computed perturbation can make them misclassify an image with high confidence, and surprisingly, the same perturbation also fools completely different networks trained on separate data. Meanwhile, probing individual hidden units turns out to be meaningless—random combinations of units reveal the same semantic information, proving

papers.title: Explaining and Harnessing Adversarial Examples
papers.pitch: Adversarial examples—inputs imperceptibly altered to fool classifiers—are not caused by model nonlinearity or overfitting, but arise from models acting too linearly in high-dimensional spaces. This insight makes adversarial training computationally practical, enabling a maxout network on MNIST to resist such attacks while improving its test error to just 0.782%.

papers.title: "Why Should I Trust You?" Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
papers.pitch: A model can be fooling you even when its test accuracy is high—LIME reveals that a classifier trained to distinguish wolves from huskies was actually just detecting snow in the background. By locally approximating any black-box model with an interpretable surrogate, this work lets non-experts identify which classifier generalizes better almost 90% of the time, simply by reading explanations of ind

papers.title: Group Normalization
papers.pitch: Batch Normalization fails catastrophically at small batch sizes, making it useless for memory-hungry tasks like object detection and video—but Group Normalization exploits the fact that channels naturally group together, computing mean and variance within channel clusters instead of across samples, and this simple switch slashes 10.6% off ImageNet error at batch size 2 while matching BN at normal

papers.title: Measuring and Improving Consistency in Pretrained Language Models
papers.pitch: Pretrained language models frequently contradict themselves when queried with simple paraphrases—predicting different facts for semantically identical prompts. Even the best model fails 39% of the time on a task deliberately simplified to help it, exposing brittle surface-form reliance rather than robust knowledge encoding.

papers.title: SayCan: Do As I Can, Not As I Say — Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.pitch: A robot paired with a large language model goes from near-total failure to 74% execution success on long-horizon tasks, simply by multiplying the model’s semantic plan scores with value functions that check what the robot can actually do in its current environment. Because this “grounding” only requires swapping in a better language model to cut errors, the paper demonstrates a direct path where a

papers.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
papers.pitch: Large transformers don't gradually get better at learning from examples—they abruptly become able to do it overnight when “induction heads” emerge, creating a visible bump in the training loss. These heads implement a simple pattern-matching algorithm that likely underlies the majority of in-context learning across model scales.

papers.title: Lightning Attention-2: A Free Lunch for Handling Unlimited Sequence Lengths in Large Language Models
papers.pitch: Linear attention promises O(n) speed but has always collapsed under the cumulative sum bottleneck in causal settings—until now. Lightning Attention-2 cracks this by tiling the computation into intra-block standard attention and inter-block linear kernels, delivering constant 38K tokens-per-second training speed from 1K to 92K context while FlashAttention-2 slows down 9×.

papers.title: ON LINEAR REPRESENTATIONS AND PRETRAINING DATA FREQUENCY IN LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.pitch: Linear representations of facts in LMs don’t just reflect model capability—they reliably snap into place once the underlying facts co-occur in pretraining data above a sharp, model-specific frequency threshold. This threshold is surprisingly consistent across training (e.g., ~1k-4k co-occurrences), and you can even read out how often a model saw a term from the quality of its internal linear encod

papers.title: MolmoAct: Action Reasoning Models that can Reason in Space
papers.pitch: MolmoAct injects explicit spatial reasoning into robot foundation models by predicting editable 2D trajectory sketches *before* outputting actions—achieving a 23.3% leap in out-of-distribution generalization without scaling data. This steerable "reasoning in space" also unlocks a +22.7% real-world bimanual task improvement over π0-FAST, proving that structured intermediate plans beat direct percep

papers.title: The End of Manual Decoding: Towards Truly End-to-End Language Models
papers.pitch: Large language models aren't truly "end-to-end"—their output quality depends on hand-tuned decoding parameters like temperature that are static and suboptimal. This paper introduces AutoDeco, a technique that lets models predict their own optimal, token-level decoding parameters on the fly, eliminating manual tuning while matching the performance of exhaustively "hacking the test set." Remarkably,

papers.title: Deep Research: A Systematic Survey
papers.pitch: Think you know LLM search? This survey reveals that today’s “deep research” agents are autonomously orchestrating multi-step workflows with persistent memory—far beyond single-shot retrieval—and yet the field still lacks a common technical vocabulary to even compare them. The authors disentangle the hype by delivering a crisp, three-phase capability roadmap and a component-by-component blueprint,

papers.title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
papers.pitch: GLM-5 shows that decoupling action generation from model training in reinforcement learning lets AI agents learn from hours-long software engineering tasks without grinding to a halt. This asynchronous design, combined with a new sparse attention mechanism, produces an open-weight model that finally matches proprietary GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.5 on real-world coding benchmarks like Vending Bench

papers.title: Deep Neural Networks for Acoustic Modeling in Speech Recognition
papers.pitch: Switching from Gaussian mixtures to deep neural networks slashes word error rates by over 30% on major benchmarks—without any tricky feature engineering—by first learning acoustic patterns from unlabeled data before refining them with labeled speech.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning Using Gaussian Fields and Harmonic Functions
papers.pitch: A unique, closed-form solution to the NP-hard problem of label propagation on graphs is achieved by relaxing the discrete Markov random field into a continuous Gaussian random field, yielding harmonic functions efficiently solved via linear equations. This formulation not only guarantees a single global optimum but also seamlessly absorbs external classifiers and class priors, with an entropy-mini

papers.title: Distance Metric Learning, with Application to Clustering with Side-Information
papers.pitch: Given just a handful of user-labeled similar and dissimilar pairs, you can learn a global distance metric that radically transforms clustering performance—turning a ~50% accuracy K-means failure into perfect 100% cluster recovery on synthetic data. This works because the metric, learned from a convex optimization, reshapes the entire input space to honor the indicated relationships, rather than me

papers.title: Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data
papers.pitch: This paper introduces TransE, an energy-based model for learning low-dimensional embeddings of multi-relational data that models relationships as translations operating on entity embeddings—if a triplet (head, label, tail) holds, then the head embedding plus the relationship vector should be close to the tail embedding (h + ℓ ≈ t).

papers.title: Rich feature hierarchies for accurate object detection and semantic segmentation
papers.pitch: Object detection had been stuck at around 30% mAP on PASCAL VOC, until R-CNN broke through by simply running a deep CNN over region proposals. The result: a 30% relative leap over the previous state of the art, proving that the ImageNet revolution could be transplanted wholesale into detection with the right glue—and kicking off the modern era of two-stage detectors.

papers.title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
papers.pitch: By sending a convnet’s internal activations back through a deconvolutional network, we can literally see what each neuron cares about—and this reveals that small changes to the first layer’s filter size and stride dramatically outperform the famous AlexNet on ImageNet.  Even more striking, the same pretrained features beat the Caltech-256 state-of-the-art by nearly 20 points without any fine-tunin

papers.title: OverFeat: Integrated Recognition, Localization and Detection using Convolutional Networks
papers.pitch: A single convolutional network can simultaneously classify, locate, and detect objects without needing background training samples or complex bootstrapping—by simply accumulating bounding box predictions across scales, the system actually uses multiple overlapping detections as a confidence boost rather than suppressing them.

papers.title: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
papers.pitch: Training on iconic, centered object photos leaves models brittle in real scenes—MS COCO reveals a nearly 2× drop in detection performance on everyday, non-iconic views compared to PASCAL VOC. Yet models trained on COCO’s dense, segmented images of 91 common objects surprisingly generalize better back to PASCAL than the reverse, proving that rich contextual variety is key to robust recognition.

papers.title: Spatial Pyramid Pooling in Deep Convolutional Networks for Visual Recognition
papers.pitch: Adding a spatial pyramid pooling layer eliminates the fixed-size input constraint in CNNs—boosting accuracy across architectures—and accelerates R-CNN object detection by up to 102× by computing convolutional features for the entire image only once.

papers.title: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge
papers.pitch: Deep learning shattered a decades-old plateau in computer vision in a single year, with a convolutional neural network halving the top-5 error rate on 1000-class image recognition. Despite this radical progress, the best machines still fell statistically short of a single trained human annotator on fine-grained categories.

papers.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
papers.pitch: Simply stacking many 3×3 convolutional layers—without exotic filter sizes or complex multi-branch topologies—produces a 16–19 layer network that crushed the previous state-of-the-art on ImageNet, winning the 2014 localization challenge and nearly matching the classification winner with just two models. This demonstrated that depth alone, achieved through small-filter stacks, is an unexpectedly pow

papers.title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.pitch: By simply feeding class labels or other auxiliary data to both the generator and discriminator, GANs become steerable—they can generate MNIST digits on command. More surprisingly, when trained on image tags, this conditional approach produces descriptive tags that were never seen during training, unlocking a one-to-many mapping from images to a rich semantic space.

papers.title: Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation
papers.pitch: By simply reshaping existing classification networks into “fully convolutional” form—replacing their final classifier layers with 1×1 convolutions—this work produced a semantic segmenter that runs 286× faster than prior state-of-the-art while simultaneously achieving a 20% relative improvement in accuracy, all without any post-processing.

papers.title: DRAW: A Recurrent Neural Network For Image Generation
papers.pitch: A generative model learns to draw digits stroke-by-stroke, refining its canvas over dozens of time steps without any explicit supervision on stroke order, simply by being forced to attend to a small foveated region at each step. This iterative, attention-based process produces images as convincing as real photos on the Street View House Numbers dataset, while the same fully differentiable attentio

papers.title: FaceNet: A Unified Embedding for Face Recognition and Clustering
papers.pitch: FaceNet achieves a record 99.63% face verification accuracy using a 128-byte embedding—roughly 100× smaller than previous deep methods—by directly optimizing Euclidean distances with a triplet loss instead of relying on intermediate classification layers. The system handles extreme pose and illumination without 2D or 3D alignment, and the paper introduces online triplet mining, which selects hard

papers.title: Fast R-CNN
papers.pitch: Fast R-CNN trains a VGG16 detector 9× faster than R-CNN and runs 213× faster at test-time while being more accurate—0.3 seconds per image versus 47. It achieves this by sharing a single convolutional feature map across all object proposals and jointly training classification and bounding box regression in one stage, eliminating the multi-stage pipeline that made prior detectors both slow and inele

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.pitch: What if you could train a top‑performing biomedical image segmenter from just 30 annotated examples — and run it in under a second? The U‑Net introduces a symmetric encoder–decoder with skip connections and a boundary‑weighted loss that, when combined with heavy elastic deformation augmentation, beats prior sliding‑window methods by a huge margin on electron‑microscopy and cell‑tracking benchmarks

papers.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
papers.pitch: A deep network learns to propose its own detection regions from convolutional features, making the proposal step nearly cost-free at just 10ms per image and eliminating the last major speed bottleneck in object detection.

papers.title: Spatial Transformer Networks
papers.pitch: CNNs can now actively warp their own feature maps—learning to center, rotate, and scale input regions on the fly, without pose labels. A single differentiable module inserted into any architecture slashes classification errors on distorted digits and fine-grained birds, effectively giving networks a built-in attention mechanism that learns spatial invariance end-to-end.

papers.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
papers.pitch: By framing object detection as a single regression from pixels to bounding boxes, YOLO achieves 155 frames per second—over twice the accuracy of prior real-time detectors—while making fewer than half the background false positives of Fast R-CNN because it sees the whole image at once.

papers.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
papers.pitch: Adding more layers to a neural network can make it perform *worse*—not just on test data, but even on the training set. This paper shows that making the layers learn residuals (the difference from the input) instead of the full mapping suddenly lets you train a 152-layer network that crushes shallower models, winning ImageNet with an ensemble error of just 3.57%.

papers.title: SqueezeNet: AlexNet-Level Accuracy with 50X Fewer Parameters and <0.5MB Model Size
papers.pitch: We built a CNN that matches AlexNet's ImageNet accuracy with 50× fewer parameters, and after compression, the entire model shrinks to under 0.5MB—510× smaller than the original—fitting directly on an FPGA. papers.title: Instance Normalization: The Missing Ingredient for Fast Stylization
papers.pitch: Simply swapping batch normalization for instance normalization in a feed-forward style transfer network closes the quality gap with slow optimization-based methods, enabling real-time stylization that finally looks as good as the original. papers.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
papers.pitch: A simple top-down architecture with lateral connections transforms a standard ConvNet into a feature pyramid that matches the accuracy of costly image pyramids while running at 6 FPS—surpassing all COCO 2016 challenge winners without bells and whistles.

papers.title: Paying More Attention to Attention: Improving the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks via Attention Transfer
papers.pitch: A powerful teacher network’s internal spatial attention maps—showing where it looks—can dramatically improve a smaller student network’s performance simply by forcing the student to mimic those maps. papers.title: Mask R-CNN
papers.pitch: Simply adding a parallel mask-prediction branch to Faster R-CNN fails badly—until you fix the misalignment introduced by RoIPool's coarse spatial quantization.  Mask R-CNN's RoIAlign layer, using bilinear interpolation at four regularly sampled points per bin, alone improves mask AP by up to 7.3 points, turning a naive extension into a top-performing instance segmentation framework that also beats

papers.title: Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
papers.pitch: What if you could turn a horse into a zebra without ever seeing a single paired example? CycleGAN achieves convincing unpaired image-to-image translation by forcing a round-trip: translate an image to the target domain and back, and it must match the original, even without ground-truth output pairs.

papers.title: Bottom-Up and Top-Down Attention for Image Captioning and Visual Question Answering
papers.pitch: Forget looking at uniform feature grids—a model that first detects objects and salient regions via Faster R-CNN (bottom-up), then learns to weight them based on the task (top-down), simultaneously sets a new state-of-the-art in image captioning and wins the 2017 VQA Challenge, all while making attention interpretable at the level of actual objects.

papers.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
papers.pitch: One-stage detectors have always been faster but less accurate than two-stage methods—this paper reveals the culprit is not architecture, but extreme foreground–background class imbalance during training. By reshaping the standard cross-entropy loss to automatically down-weight easy examples, a simple dense detector suddenly matches the speed of one-stage models while beating all state-of-the-art t

papers.title: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks
papers.pitch: By simply adding a lightweight “squeeze-and-excitation” block that learns to weight channels based on global context, a ResNet-50 can outperform the much deeper ResNet-101 on ImageNet with negligible extra cost. This recalibration mechanism, which adaptively emphasizes informative features and suppresses less useful ones, won the ILSVRC 2017 classification challenge, slashing the top-5 error by ~2

papers.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning by Predicting Image Rotations
papers.pitch: What if simply teaching a network to detect whether an image has been rotated forces it to understand objects at a semantic level? This paper demonstrates that this deceptively simple pretext task trains ConvNets to recognize high-level object categories and canonical orientations, closing the gap with supervised pre-training to just 2.4 mAP points on PASCAL VOC detection—without using a single hu

papers.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.pitch: Injecting noise and learned style transformations at each layer forces the generator to automatically separate global pose from local hair placement, without supervision. This redesign not only makes faces more realistic than previous GANs but also yields a vastly more linear, navigable latent space.

papers.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
papers.pitch: MoCo’s unsupervised pre-training surprisingly beats supervised ImageNet pretraining on 7 detection and segmentation benchmarks, with gains as large as +4.9 AP₇₅ on VOC. It achieves this by treating contrastive learning as dictionary look-up, using a momentum encoder and a dynamic queue to build a large, consistent key set on-the-fly without massive batches.

papers.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
papers.pitch: SimCLR shows you can match a fully supervised ResNet-50 on ImageNet using self-supervised contrastive learning with no specialized architecture or memory bank—just a brutally simple recipe of stronger data augmentation, a small nonlinear projection head, and very large batch sizes. papers.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
papers.pitch: A simple neural network weighing just 5 MB can reconstruct photorealistic 3D scenes from just a few dozen photos—outperforming prior work by up to 9 dB while achieving a 3000× compression ratio over traditional explicit volumetric grids.

papers.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
papers.pitch: DETR eliminates the entire postprocessing stack of modern object detectors—anchors, region proposals, and non-maximum suppression—by reformulating detection as a set prediction problem and solving it with a transformer. It matches the accuracy of heavily‑engineered baselines like Faster R‑CNN while being a fraction of the conceptual and implementation complexity.

papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.pitch: A pure Transformer matching state-of-the-art CNNs on ImageNet sounds impossible—until you feed it 300 million images. ViT shows that the right training scale can override the need for convolutional inductive biases, achieving top results with far less compute.

papers.title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention
papers.pitch: Contrary to earlier claims, pure vision transformers can be trained to high accuracy on just ImageNet without external data—DeiT achieves 83.1% on a single machine in under 3 days. papers.title: Pyramid Vision Transformer: A Versatile Backbone for Dense Prediction without Convolutions
papers.pitch: A pyramid-structured Vision Transformer eclipses ResNets as a backbone for object detection and segmentation—PVT-Small delivers 40.4 AP on COCO with RetinaNet, a 4-point leap over ResNet50 at fewer parameters. This is the first pure Transformer to natively produce multi-scale features, eliminating convolutions entirely while outperforming heavily engineered CNN backbones.

papers.title: Coordinate Attention for Efficient Mobile Network Design
papers.pitch: Standard channel attention (like SE blocks) throws away positional information by using 2D global pooling—a surprisingly costly omission for mobile networks, where coordinate attention recovers it by factorizing pooling into two 1D feature encodings along horizontal and vertical directions. papers.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
papers.pitch: Swin Transformer achieves linear computational complexity relative to image size, smashing previous state-of-the-art detection and segmentation records by over +2.5 points across the board, by confining self-attention to local windows that shift between layers. This hierarchical design finally makes Transformers practical as general-purpose vision backbones for dense prediction tasks.

papers.title: Emerging Properties in Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.pitch: Self-supervised ViTs spontaneously learn to segment objects, with attention maps directly delineating boundaries—without any labels. These same features also achieve 78.3% ImageNet top-1 accuracy using only a k-NN classifier, no fine-tuning required.

papers.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision
papers.pitch: A vision model built solely from multi-layer perceptrons—no convolutions, no self-attention—matches the performance of state-of-the-art CNNs and Transformers when trained on massive datasets, proving that neither architectural prior is necessary for competitive image classification. papers.title: Florence: A New Foundation Model for Computer Vision
papers.pitch: Florence smashes the long-held assumption that computer vision must remain fragmented across tasks, hitting 83.74% zero-shot top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K by training a single model on 900 million image-text pairs to span classification, detection, VQA, and video action recognition simultaneously. This single model rivals or beats specialized systems on 44 benchmarks, proving that a unified visual

papers.title: A ConvNet for the 2020s
papers.pitch: A pure ConvNet can match vision Transformers by simply modernizing its design—no attention needed. The resulting ConvNeXt family outperforms Swin Transformers on COCO and ADE20K while being simpler and faster.

papers.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
papers.pitch: Simply swapping the U-Net in a latent diffusion model for a standard Vision Transformer (ViT) yields state-of-the-art image generation — and the resulting Diffusion Transformers are so compute-efficient that a model with 10x fewer Gflops beats heavily engineered U-Net baselines like ADM. papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.pitch: A single segmentation model, prompted by a mere point, matches or beats fully supervised specialists across 23 unseen datasets without any fine-tuning. Trained on 1 billion auto-generated masks, it transforms segmentation from a task-specific slog into a general, prompt-driven capability.

papers.title: Replacing softmax with ReLU in Vision Transformers
papers.pitch: Vision transformers don’t need softmax to scale—just applying ReLU to attention scores and dividing by sequence length matches softmax accuracy across model sizes. This simple tweak eliminates exponentials and cross-sequence normalization, unlocking new parallelization strategies.

papers.title: ConvNets Match Vision Transformers at Scale
papers.pitch: A pure convolutional network, pre-trained on a 4-billion image dataset, matches the scaling power of Vision Transformers—a 90.4% ImageNet top‑1 result disproves the widely held belief that ConvNets lose out at web-scale.

papers.title: Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2)
papers.pitch: SAM 2 takes the 'segment anything' idea from images to video, and in doing so actually becomes a *better* image segmentor: it's 6× faster than the original SAM while being more accurate, because its streaming memory architecture—designed for tracking objects across frames—generalizes back to static images by simply leaving the memory empty. papers.title:
Building and better understanding vision-language models: insights and
  future directions
papers.pitch: A simple VLM built on Llama 3.1 can jump 13.7 points on DocVQA to 87.7 just by training on a massive, automatically curated QA dataset—no architectural complexity needed. The paper further shows that even a 0.7B model trained on this synthetic data can match generalist 8B models at document understanding, challenging the costly race for ever-larger unimodal backbones.

Document Parsing Unveiled: Techniques, Challenges, and Prospects for
  Structured Information Extraction
papers.pitch: Modern VLMs can read documents but still corrupt mathematical formulas and misorder text — a problem this survey reveals stems not from model capacity, but from naive end-to-end decoding that ignores page structure. The authors show modular pipelines decisively beat monolithic models on fine-grained accuracy benchmarks, making structure-aware decomposition the critical missing link.

papers.title: Parallelized Autoregressive Visual Generation
papers.pitch: Conventional wisdom says autoregressive models must generate visual tokens one-by-one, but this paper reveals that spatially distant tokens carry such weak dependencies that they can be safely predicted in parallel, enabling a 9.5× speedup without architectural changes—simply by reorganizing the prediction order to keep local neighbors sequential while batching far-apart tokens together.

papers.title: DINOv3
papers.pitch: DINOv3 reveals that scaling self-supervised vision models past 1B parameters causes their dense feature maps to collapse during training—a previously undiagnosed failure mode that is directly solved by a new 'Gram anchoring' regularization. papers.title: Autoregressive Universal Video Segmentation Model
papers.pitch: AUSM treats video segmentation like language modeling—predicting masks frame by frame—and uses a constant-size spatial state to unify prompted and unprompted tasks, outperforming prior universal models by 8.7 points on YouTube-VOS 2018 while training 2.5× faster than iterative methods.

papers.title: AToken: A Unified Tokenizer for Vision
papers.pitch: For the first time, a single transformer tokenizer can master both high-fidelity reconstruction and semantic understanding across images, videos, and 3D assets without adversarial training. By mapping everything into a shared 4D latent space, ATOKEN shows that unifying vision modalities no longer requires trading off generation quality against recognition accuracy.

papers.title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
papers.pitch: DeepSeek-OCR achieves 97% OCR precision by using up to 10x fewer vision tokens than text tokens, showing that document pages can be optically compressed into compact representations. Remarkably, it still retains 60% accuracy even at a brutal 20x compression ratio, challenging the assumption that high-resolution tokens are always needed for text-heavy tasks. papers.title: Depth Anything 3: Recovering the Visual Space from Any Views
papers.pitch: A single vanilla transformer predicting only depth and ray maps outperforms all specialized models across monocular depth, any-view geometry, and camera pose estimation—surpassing prior SOTA VGGT by 35.7% in pose accuracy while requiring no architectural specialization or multi-task learning.

papers.title: Molmo2: Open Weights and Data for Vision-Language Models with Video Understanding and Grounding
papers.pitch: An open 8B vision-language model, trained entirely without proprietary model distillation, not only matches state-of-the-art open video understanding but introduces pixel-level video pointing and tracking capabilities that beat Gemini 3 Pro—achieving 38.4 vs. 20.0 F1 on pointing—proving high-quality, human-collected spatio-temporal data can leapfrog closed-source distillation.

papers.title: DeCAF: A Deep Convolutional Activation Feature for Generic Visual Recognition
papers.pitch: Features from a single deep network trained only on ImageNet object categories transfer astonishingly well to entirely different visual tasks—without any fine-tuning, a linear classifier on these frozen activations crushes prior state-of-the-art on scene recognition, fine-grained bird classification, and domain adaptation. papers.title: DeepFace: Closing the Gap to Human-Level Performance in Face Verification
papers.pitch: A deep network with over 120 million locally connected parameters, trained on 4.4 million faces and paired with precise 3D alignment, achieves 97.35% accuracy on LFW—slashing the previous error rate by more than 27% and effectively matching human performance.

papers.title: Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection
papers.pitch: For reliable human detection, discarding fine-scale edge details in favor of smoother features is a critical mistake—blurring the image or gradients before computing orientation histograms actually increases false positives by over an order of magnitude. papers.title: A Global Geometric Framework for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction
papers.pitch: The straight-line distance between two face photos taken from opposite angles is tiny in pixel space, yet our brain effortlessly sees them as far apart in pose—Isomap reveals this hidden perceptual manifold by treating the data like a curved universe where shortest paths must follow the surface, not cut across empty space.

papers.title: Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders
papers.pitch: A gated convolutional PixelCNN matches the log-likelihood of a much slower recurrent PixelRNN by stacking separate vertical and horizontal convolutions to eliminate blind spots. By conditioning the same model on a face embedding from a single photo, it can generate entirely novel portraits of that person with varied poses, expressions, and lighting.

papers.title: Distinctive Image Features from Scale-Invariant Keypoints
papers.pitch: A single image feature can be matched correctly against a database of 40,000 features with over 90% reliability, even under substantial viewpoint change and noise, by discarding nearly all false matches with a simple distance ratio test. papers.title: On Spectral Clustering: Analysis and an Algorithm
papers.pitch: A simple spectral algorithm using k eigenvectors achieves near-perfect clustering on intertwined, concentric, and non-convex structures where K-means fails completely. The paper provides the first rigorous proof linking clustering success to the eigengap, showing that when the gap between λ_k and λ_{k+1} is large, the embedded points form tight, separated clusters even under noise.

papers.title: Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features
papers.pitch: A face detector can achieve real-time speed without sacrificing accuracy by combining simple rectangular features evaluated in constant time with a cascade that rejects most image regions after evaluating just a handful of features—running at 15 frames per second on a single grayscale image from 2001 hardware.
